title: Our Cat LOVES This  She Is Not Too Sure Of The Fan Yet But..
text:
WARNING: This is an in depth review to help with making an informed buying decision. If you prefer a brief summary, see section marked THE BOTTOM LINE
-----------------------------------------
We had a cat who was so independent I never would have thought to buy something like this for him. Then we rescued a little kitty from a difficult living situation, and she is the antithesis of our other cat who has now passed. She LOVES to be on top of us and whatever we are doing. Let's take a look at this carrier.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This carrier is really cool. It has a GREAT BIG WINDOW in it which is better than the last one we had used for her. It has side vents, and rubberized mesh at the back edges. There are vents on the bottom and top of window area too.

CAN KITTY LOOK AROUND?
The side windows and front window give a perfect chance for the cat to look around anywhere she wants to see.

FLOOR
Our last carrier had a floor mat in it, but this one is flat on the bottom and seems very sturdy and comfortable.

HANDLE
The top handle is padded and easy to carry if you need to.

SHOULDER STRAPS
The shoulder straps on this are padded and curved, and is comfortable to wear.

BASE
The base stands up on its own. This is VERY handy in that we unzip the backpack and the back drops down like a platform she can go up to get into the carrier.

REFLECTIVE
There is a band of reflective tape on the shoulder straps for reflection.

FAN
There is a place for the power bank to put in so the fan will connect, but at this point, our cat loves the carrier, but she is not too sure on the fan movement of air yet. I am slowly getting her used to it.

SO DOES THE CAT ACTUALLY LIKE THIS?
I have to tell you, we have only had the cat in this a few times and this morning, we opened the back and left it on the ground. She ran right over, sat in place and waited to be zipped in. After only being worn for about 15 minutes, we had to put her down as we were doing something she could not be on our backs for. When we opened the zipper, she refused to get out at first. She wanted to stay!

THE BOTTOM LINE
This backpack is a fantastic gizmo if you have a cat that loves to be with you but is underfoot all of the time. It helps keep them close to you while allowing you to do what you need to do without tripping on him/her. This backpack is a thrill for our cat. She loves it and gets in it willingly. The only time she does not like it is when she is outside in it as she is an indoor/outdoor cat and loves to do her own thing when outside.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is fabulous. I am SO GLAD to have it. It is solving a problem for us (clingy cat) so that kitty has her together time and then goes out on her own feeling all happy.

title: Life saver must have for sick pup
text:
My little Furbaby had to take antibiotics for a UTI and I knew it might cause gastrointestinal issues (Mud Butt ) .I thought I’d better get something bigger and better than the usual puppy pads we use regularly. I looked for a big size and found this . It’s such a generous size , perfect to cover the area in my bed where my lil guy sleeps . The first night was rough , he puked and this pad caught it all . It saved me having puke on my bed . Being in the middle of the night I cleaned up the mess and folded the dirty area over and rolled it up a bit so the dirty part was all gone and only the clean part of the pad was left . The next miring I washed and dried the pad and that went great . Washed up like new . Next 2 days went fine but on day 3 in the middle of the night I heard him get up and the other end of him started having trouble. What a mess !!! It was so bad . Some of it was on the disposable puppy pads but not all on it . Idk what would have if I didn’t have this pad ! Geeze it really performed beyond any expectations I had . The worst of it wiped up so easy . Then in the washer it went and came out clean like nothing happened 6 hrs earlier . My dog is over the worst of it and I’m so thankful I had this to use while the worst side effects were happening. I really would have had to throw away my bed and mattress pad if I had not had this . I’m forever a fan of this puppy /whelping pad . I wish I knew this existed years ago when my kids were little , I know it’s made for animals but it would be fantastic to use for kids too ! For doing arts and crafts or to sit on inside or even outside with coated bottom . I’m seriously considering sending my dad and sister a couple of these for their dogs to sleep on . It had a coupon that took a bit off the total and made it a fair price . Affordable for sure . It shipped faster then it said it would thank goodness and I had it in place when it mattered the most . I will update this review once Iv washed it a bunch and see how it holds up . I feel like Iv gotten my monies worth out of it already but if it lasted a long time thru tons of washings I would not be mad about it at all . It also helped keep
My little guy warm . I pushed some of the extra fabric around his body while he was laying down feeling bad and it helped him be warm and comfortable. He usually shares my blanket with me but with him having explosive Diarrhea he had to stay on this and couldn’t share my blanket and I didn’t want him to be cold so I used the pad to keep him warm and it still protected my bed from disaster.

title: BOTTOMLINE if you use PINE PELLETS - DON'T count on dimensions - TOO SMALL for my SMALL cat
text:
IN THEORY, great idea. In practice, not as much.

I GET this is meant for clay clumping litter, but many of us like pine pellets better.

IF one doesn't SIFT in some way, it's very difficult to not dump GOOD pellets along with those turned to sawdust when urine hits them.

This works the opposite way if you use pellets. Rather than the clumps you want to get RID of, in the sifting tray, the GOOD pellets stay in the tray and sawdust falls through.

PROS:

LOOKS - Attractive looking the way boxes stack, liked the colors.

SIFTER - This is a pro and a con. I found just shaking it didn't work well and needed to use the scooper to move around the pine pellet litter (that's the only litter I like for my cat)
BUT it does work.

BIGGEST PRO is that I don't waste litter. Using non clumping pine pellet, you can easily waste too much trying to remove urine as it turns to sawdust.

IF you use pine pellets and don't want to WASTE, it's important to sift it somehow.

CONS:

NOT BIG ENOUGH! - I have a fairly small cat, not full grown. She's about 16 inches long, not counting tail.
She was putting her paws on the rim of the litter box and was going to the bathroom standing like that.

THE DIMENSIONS given are DECEIVING! They SAID they were the size of her previous litter tray. The dimensions are for the SIFTER which is bigger than the trays, it sticks out around the trays.

CAN'T really just SHAKE the sifter. I got sawdust all around the box. And takes too long (and I just started using this set up two days ago, and it's one small cat) to try too sift, using the scoop to spread out along sifter faster, but kind of negates part of the reason for sifter.

YOU STILL need to just pick up the poo out of the box if you use pellets. Not a big deal for my one small cat, but it's another step.

ALSO at some point you need to disinfect the sifter. You're dumping a litter box of used and still pellets going through it. Hardly germ free and I leave it in my bathroom near her litter box.

BOTTOMLINE: I SAVED my plain old, but large, litter box. I will keep that and just use the sifter and one of the trays to dump out pellets and sawdust and separate, but that takes up more room. I am looking at getting a bigger sifting box, I see Petco has an extra large one available on Amazon. In the meantime, my small bathroom is being taken up with one large regular cat pan litter box, the sifter and one of the cat pans that came with the sifter.

BOTTOMLINE: DO NOT trust the dimensions. My cat isn't large and wasn't big enough for her. IF it had been a LARGER size (I HOPE Arm and Hammer will make one at some point), this would likely have been five stars.

text: I love salmon and have a small piece along with a small salad a few times a week for lunch.  I have a dog and 2 cats who also love salmon  and believe me, they're all over me when I have salmon for lunch. Each piece is hard-I did attempt to crumble some on top of the cat's food but it was just too hard. So now I break a piece off and dunk it in water for a bit to soften it up and that REALLY helps. I"m then able to easily break it into small pieces and put some on top of the cat's dry food as a treat.  And this couldn't have come at a better time.  One of our cats, appropriately named Miss Piggy, needs to lose 2-3lbs per the vet.  She and our other cat Squeaky are now eating dry cat food the vet recommended to help with Piggy's weight loss goal. Naturally, they both HATE the new cat food. lol.  But when I sprinkle it with some Whole Life salmon fillet pieces, they go bonkers and devour the new cat food.  Naturally, our dog Mac sees this and wants some as well so I must also moisten a piece of the salmon fillet and put it on top of his dog food.  (Can you tell our furbabies are spoiled? lol) I've timed it so when i give the animals their Whole Life salmon, I take MY salmon and salad and go into another room, close the door and eat in peace without the animals begging me to share my lunch!  The fillets actually came in handy a few days ago...I had to give Mac 1/2 Benadryl pill but I hadn't been to the grocery store -we were out of peanut butter which where I usually hide a pill when he needs to take one. My one 'beef' with these fillets is that all 6 are vacuum sealed together.  While its not the end of the world, I do wish each fillet was individually sealed.  There is a bit of a scent to these fillets-reminds me of goldfish flakes I used to feed my pet goldfish when I was a kid. lol. title: Really cute, cat-friendly, but misses the target
text:
We bought two of these birds for our kitty cats. I think Hartz could have done better though.

The look is great - like a mini-pheasant, which immediately grabbed both cats' attention.
The chirp is very loud. I SAID, THE CHIRP IS VERY LOUD! At least ours were! Yikes - sort of like a bird with a megaphone! It got on my nerves, but didn't seem to bother the cats that I could tell. (They might have been wishing for ear plugs, but who knows.) Annoyance factor for me was slightly less than the battery-operated chimp with the clapping cymbals (but I can take the batteries out of the chimp).

Now the downside - the interest lasts about as long as it is making noise.
It makes noise upon impact with something, and it takes a fairly hard impact to get it chirping. Slapping against your hand is the best way, or slapping it on a hard surface. However, unless your cats are different than the two we have, the cats will not be able to turn on the chirping themselves. You know how cats like to grab and toss things like this type of toy into the air? You'd think the mechanism would have been made sensitive enough to turn on when it hit the floor. Not so - the cats are not strong enough to turn this bird's sound on. It will take YOUR interaction.

Now, I love to play with the cats and don't have a problem with it. However, I thought this would be a cute toy to keep them busy while I was on the computer. Instead, it was either brought back to me to slap/throw it again (yes, one of our cats acts like a dog and retrieves toys), or was left on the floor as soon as it stopped chirping. They did carry them around the first day or two, but that novelty wore off uber fast. Right now, I think one is laying dormant under our china closet, and I don't know where Bird 2 is. The cats don't really care either. They lost interest right away.

If Hartz revamps these and makes the chirp-triggering mechanism more sensitive, then this toy would be a winner. You can't deny it looks great. But, the cats got as bored as I did, because the noise is part of the appeal. It goes silent, then it is no longer a prize to be obtained. So, I think you can do better than this toy for your favorite kitty.

text:
It's still early on for me, but so far I am liking this fish tank. I have the vertical 5 gallon. It has been years since I have had a fish tank. I normally had the 10 or 50 gallon horizontal style. They just took up too much room and was too much work. I was terrible at keeping fish alive. I have been missing the serenity of gazing into a fish tank, so I have been considering one if I could find a spot for a small one. When I saw this vertical one come up as an option, I knew I had to try it out.

Instead of taking up width it is taking up height. I like that there are lots of accessories available. I looked online to determine how much gravel I would need (5 lbs for 5 gallons). I used a little less since it is a more narrow design. I added in some other GloFish items- rocks, fake sea anemone, plants, etc.. I'm giving the water a few days to settle before I add actual fish to it. I was going to wait to review until later in the week, but I was eager to make comments. I'll be sure to add pics soon. (EDIT: added 6 male guppies to tank, and added pics here)

The set up is easy. There isn't much to do. It comes with filter system and lights. Both are attached in same spot. There is a glass lid that gets set on top. Good thing, since I have 4 seriously curious cats. Pretty sure this system will be secure from prying paws once the live fish go in. Pretty sure..

The tank is placed on a short base (included). It isn't attached, just placed on top. It is sturdy and has a rubber grip to keep it from sliding off. I imagine it would be fine not using the base.

Lights turned on create a cool look on the accessories I picked up. So awesome. Natural, Bright blue, low blue, black/purple light, off.

I'm excited to have a fish tank again, even if it is smaller than I am used to. I have it at my home desk (edit: moved it into my family room) so I can look at it easily. And my cats.

I'll keep playing around with this thing and I will be sure to come back to update as I learn more.

Edit: still Loving it. Back wall on tank is black, so no need for background paper (not ability to add it). I definitely recommend glofish accessories if wanting to use purple light. I am using regular guppies, but there are fish out there that will pick up black light effect.

title: This Is A Lifesaver No Joke!
text:
I read all the reviews and worried about using a collar on my Min Pin service dog. I saw the photos of a dog who got a rash and read reviews that it had no effect on other small dogs. I have never used a collar of any kind on my dog and worried that it might be uncomfortable. However, I became desperate due to his increasing anxiety with construction around us. He began whining and hiding and was inconsistent with his tasks that he usually loves to perform for me. A veterinary behaviorist evaluated him and recommended an Adaptil Collar but I tried the spray instead. When the spray helped, I ordered an Adaptil Diffuser--which also helps indoors. But suddenly my dog began barking at strangers and unfamiliar dogs. He lost interest in his favorite treats and pastimes. I got help from his trainer and tried behavioral training for the triggers. Things were improving a bit then yesterday, just before the collar arrived, something frightened him (I don't know what) and he managed to escape from his harness and run naked through a crowded and heavily trafficked shopping plaza where I had just undergone a medical procedure. I prayed if I ever got my dog back, through a miracle, I would use the Adaptil collar when it arrived. It is truly a miracle that I have my dog back. He was so spooked that he didn't come when I called. He ran up to a building across heavy traffic and a woman brought him into her office, when she saw him running on the railed deck. Luckily, her office was below a dog groomer's place and the groomer was helping me look for my dog. I was still sedated from the medical procedure, and in a wheelchair, but the able-bodied groomer called my dog's name and whistled for him to come. The woman who had my dog heard the man call and returned my dog to me just in time for dial-a-ride to take us home.

I have never used a collar on any animal and worried this would be difficult. It is super easy. There are also videos on YouTube that demonstrate.

I got the small size made for dogs and puppies, recommended for his breed, and it fits perfectly.

He loved the scent the minute I opened the box (I can't smell anything) and even bent his head so I could slip it on. You slip it over their head and adjust it afterwards.

The new upstairs neighbor was making a lot of noise moving in but my dog didn't whine or hide. He cuddled up beside me, closed his eyes, and went to sleep amid all the commotion.

I know there are other calming collars out there but I haven't tried them. I'm sticking to what works. Sentry makes a calming collar that a friend recommended--I didn't like the color for my boy dog and don't want to smell lavender. Plus, his veterinary behaviorist and his vet only recommend Adaptil.

The instructions say keep it on at all times except when grooming. It is very lightweight, soft and pliable and will break free if caught (a concern I had).

It may not work for every dog but if you are desperate like I was, try it. Read the directions. Follow the directions. Don't make the collar too loose or too tight (should be able to insert 2 fingers). If too loose it won't work because depends upon the dog's body heat. And if too loose or too tight it might cause irritation from twisting, turning and rubbing.

So far it works. The next step would have been prescription Paxil--I don't want my fur baby medicated.

It works but remember it's not all we are doing. My dog has regular training with a service dog trainer and we also use the Adaptil spray and Adaptil diffuser. Perhaps it's working because it's part of a whole anti-anxiety program designed by his veterinary behaviorist, who knows and understands him.

title: Good'n'Fun Pork Chews? My Dog Says No
text:
Dogs love treats and they especially love treats that are meaty or at least flavored like meat. This was enough to convince me and my vizla/shepherd mixed breed to give Good-n-Fun Pork Chews a try.

This dog treat is made to be chewy and long- lasting, keeping dogs occupied and happy. Straight from the package, they emit a strong, chemical like aroma that is not very appealing. True, other dog treats stink also, but most dog treats that claim to be meat flavored at least smell like meat. These have an odd smell and I wasn’t sure my dog would take to them.

Once I removed the first stick, my dog came running over so apparently he doesn’t find the smell that bad. He took the treat and headed to the carpeting, where he proceeded to chew. These chews are meant to keep a dog chewing and occupied for a while and my dog did spend a good deal of time with his. But then something unusual happened: He dropped the chew and started doing something else. I went and picked it up and he did react, demanding I give it back to him. But once I walked away, he dropped the chew again. He apparently didn’t want me to have it, but he also didn’t really want it that badly for himself.

A couple of days later, the chew is still lying there, on the carpet. I finally took it and discarded since it was clear this treat just wasn’t to my dogs liking. He acted the same way when presented with another chew from the package. I don’t know if I got a pack that was lower quality or what, but it is clear that my dog doesn’t deem these treats worthy for canine consumption and for that reason, I have to give them a thumbs- down rating. They might work for your dog, if you’re willing to take the chance. But they are a no- go for my 2 year old mixed breed and they are not a treat I would purchase again.

It just now arrived and my husband brought it back to the room that Camo and I were playing. As soon as I opened the bag of small squeaky toys Camo was so excited. As I was opening one of the individual bags to get it out Camo was going nuts because it was taking me to long. That's when he made it clear to me that he also liked the clear plastic bags that each one came in. Once he does make it to the stuffed toys that when I realized his teething had gotten worse and these toys were perfect!
They're so soft and have a small squeaker that he can finally squeak a toy with his mouth. Plus they're durable enough for him to play with until his teething is done, but just in case he does get to the stuffing I can order more of these at a price that makes him feel better with one click on Amazon.

text:
I have two large, lazy cats that do manage to find enough energy to sharpen their claws, usually on the designated scratching posts but occasionally on the carpet. I was curious to see how well this scratching station would hold up. I have a concise answer - it lasted a week.

This is a cardboard-based scratching pad, with strips of emery board between the cardboard. This is not a bad approach and it seems like a good solution for cats to sharpen their claws.

However, the cardboard is glued down insecurely so when the cat does sit on it to sharpen claws, the cardboard breaks loose and the whole thing is compromised.

It took my cats a week to pull the cardboard off this scratch pad, and they only occasionally used it, preferring their older scratching post. That’s unacceptable. More care should have been put into construction, even if it meant costing slightly more. I cannot recommend this solution, based on how briefly it lasted. title: Works wonders
text:
I have a 65lb male Boxer who had never had his nails trimmed in his entire life. He became a member of my family a little over a year ago and I have been trying desperately to figure out a way to shorten his nails for both his comfort and my sanity (his clicking on my floors is enough to drive someone up a wall!).

The problem I encountered was that his quicks were right to the end of his nails (as is to be expected in his case). So, I know that I need to trim his nails frequently in order to encourage the quicks to recede up the nails. I have tried guillotine style trimmers and these are nothing but torture for both of us (I cannot keep a good grip on the wide handles and they are nothing but pinchers in his eyes as they apply too much pinching and not enough cutting). I have also requested that my vet help me out and, sadly, their idea of a nail trim is to use a pair of guillotine trimmers - no thank you.

So, after some desperate searching, I found and purchased this Dremel based on reviews here on Amazon and other pet sites. It arrived in a timely fashion and the packaging was easy to open. I did have to go online to find better instructions on how to insert the sandpaper band (the included instructions appear to be written by someone who is assuming the consumer is a Dremel wiz and already knows how to do everything - very annoying!). Once that hurdle was jumped, I tested the unit out on myself to see exactly what my dog will be experiencing. This tool is very powerful and can be extremely accurate, depending on the angle at which you hold it. I introduced my dog to it by letting him smell it, then turned it on and let him investigate and learn the sounds of both speeds. We seem to like the lower speed for most of the time and the higher speed for the initial sanding of the leading edge of the nails. In our case, it is too easy to go to short thus sanding into his quicks and making him bleed - so we are pleased with using the lower speed.

Overall, I can see this product serving its purpose - we simply have to be patient as encouraging quicks to recede can be a very time consuming project. Yet I have no doubts that I finally have the right tool for the task at hand. My dog seems to handle the Dremel very well (although I think it is because he is just an attention lover).. he will lie on the floor on his back and not fuss at all while I do each foot in succession. He is a little touchy on the back feet, but I think it is just him being slightly ticklish. Highly recommended by both human and Boxer alike!

title: Sturdy climber, real carpet, cat approved
text:
--I just got this today! It came fully assembled in a big, sturdy box. The cat perch was easy to slide out. ((Before you destroy the box, it could easily be repurposed as an additional feline enrichment play item.)) I placed it near a corner that I have a few of their kitty climbers set up (basically to make my own mega cat tree without it being one unit that cant be moved around much). Placing it among the familiar items is just to introduce them to the brand new item, and to pique curiosity. That is my advice to you, especially if no one is taking an interest in it at first. Eventually I will find a new location for it. Next, and also a bit of advice, was to sprinkle on a generous dose of cat nip. One by one each of our four adult cats came over to check out the new item (ages ranging from 6-17). They jumped on it, sniffed it, got a good whiff of cat nip, scratched at the carpet, chewed on the feather, rubbed up on it, etc. Our two young labs were also intrigued. I will be adding pictures of everyone to show scale, and to show the material it is made of.
--I didn't notice it in the description, but I see it now, is that attached is a very nice feather toy that dangles under top perch. Feathers are a favorite in this household, so this was a pleasant surprise. Nice touch!! (now hopefully my labs leave it alone!)
--After looking at reviews, I chose this based on how sturdy it appeared, and that it uses wood composite (oriented strand board?) instead of, and real carpeting over short napped/smooth material that some climbers have (that my cats don't love). It was as nice as expected, as sturdy as I hoped for (this thing is not going to just tip over during a cat running up or down it) and the cats LOVE the feel of the REAL carpeting. The sisal wrapped scratching areas are higher up on the climber which shows that the designer has cats or at least understands cats. Additionally, the two perches are positioned in such a manner that it can easily be climbed up (or used as a climber to get to other high spaces). This is good use of space. The spacing between the two perches is adequate for cats to sit, sleep or play. The space between base and lowest perch has the least amount of space, but it is an area that is often dismissed anyway (though appears still enough room for a cat to crawl through). I had seen the similar sized but slightly different design of the other Large perch/condo offered by this company, and it was the spacing between each level that bought me to buying this one. The other had an additional perch, but given that they are same height, the spacing between each is less, and I am thinking most cats would prefer a little more space and less cramped feel. I am glad I went with this one.
--The other aspect that I like is that each perch has three low sides to it. It offers enough material to feel cozy, yet not so much that it hinders climbing or play behavior. The top perch is wide with short depth, and the bottom perch is more narrow but much longer/deeper. Both offer a lot of space without infringing on the other. While I don't see the base as hanging out/sleeping space, it is conducive to floor play, or toy storage. I can picture my cats batting toys around the base, or using the frame to pull themselves around.
--I will be curious how long the sisal twine stays attached, as well as the carpet. It appears to be attached well, but time will tell.
--Pleasant neutral color- beige.
--This would also be nice and sturdy for small dogs. The dimensions of the unit and the perches are listed in the description, and this one would be quite adequate for a small to small/med dog to sit on.

title: It works, but it isn't the cats' favorite way to get brushed!
text:
We got one of these to see if it would really do any good for grooming our cats.
One cat would let us brush him all day if we could, but our little girl? Well, she
fights every single grooming effort you make, whether it is a toenail trim or a brushing.

We also have a furminator and various wire bristled brushes. I wanted to try this and see
if I could even rub it over our girl cat while she was passing by! Ha!

This does work at getting loose surface hair. It does NOT go down and get the dander-making
coat that most cats have - it stays on the surface. What we found that it also does a nice job on
is after brushing with a bristle-style brush, I go over the kitty with this glove. It pulls all the hair
that was loose on top, as well as hair loosened from the other grooming.

It is reasonably easy to clean, if you "roll" the hair off. If you try to pick at sections, you'll
have a mess.

This also does a good job on furniture, believe it or not. I "brushed" my office chair, which is
a favorite place for our boy cat to lounge. I was able to get a lot of loose hair off the chair
with this glove.

So, is it the cats' favorite way to get brushed? Nope. Neither one cares for it much, even though
the male will tolerate it. Is it my favorite? Nope - it doesn't take off enough hair to be useful.
But, it is still a nice way to spend time with your cat, and many cats will enjoy the extra attention,
no matter what you are using. As long as you are not rough or hard while using this, it seems like it
would be a little massaging and decent for them.
(PS - ours came in red.)

We use oko cat litter, the super soft natural wood. I love the bigger pellets of pine but our cat, little miss particular, started to pee around the house so we had to switch back to a smaller and finer litter.

title: UPDATED REVIEW... 9 years later!!!
text:
I have used these way more than even some 'backyard breeder' would because I use them 'off label' for my medically fragile, PDD, adult child (adult bladder, young child lack of control). I use them on his bed, as he is a 'mover and shaker' in his bed... the small human bed pads just don't stay under him. I use them on my sofa; I left one at my parents' to use on their sofa. They wash with minimal off-balancing-spin in my 5.1cu washer (bulky cycle does better than deep water for me).
They do - because they're made for newborn puppies - reflect body heat. Which might be great for someone elderly who stays cold. My son runs like a furnace. A broken, overheating furnace. I put small, quilted cotton throws that I got $5 each on clearance on top of the shell pads and that does make a difference. The ones I have are the ones I last bought 9+ years ago here off Amazon. The rubber backing has only washed off on the ones I bought 11 years ago but, to be fair, I only had those 2 for 2 years and washed them nearly every day.
********************
(Original Review) Having a 'perpetual' child (special needs/medically fragile/developmentally delayed), I've used just about every bed pad known to mankind: They're all pretty good, but none are large enough for more than a twin bed or crib. My 'big kid' needs more than a twin sized bed - he's very much a traveler when he's in bed (imagine how two year olds are all over a bed...now imagine a two year old the size of an adult all over the bed) and he ALWAYS came off the twin sized ones, whether it was up or sideways; he even manages to get along the edge of the bed and then have his accident down the side of the bed). This size will fit the top of a king size mattress, so it hangs off the sides of a full and definitely is full coverage on a queen. Another plus, for me, is if you don't want to bleach bed pads to remove urine stains, these can be washed with the detergent of your choice, and you know they are clean without a dingy yellow cast that only bleach can remove. If there is a detraction from these, it is that the fabric on the back side is knit so so tight, to keep anything from going through, that it kind of makes your own body heat radiate back up. In other words, they can be warmish - even under a quality sheet. For us, though, that's not an issue. I have MANY of these pads, so if there is an accident in the middle of the night, he can be changed and the bed pad can be swapped without too much hassle. When you do need to launder, throw 'em in the washer as if they were a load of towels - they're durable enough for multiple washings on even a whites setting (hot water, etc.). Price is, on a price per square inch basis, much better than the white cottony bed pads.

title: WOW- What a PERFECT Snack For Our Cats
text:
We are big supporters of raw foods for cats. We have developed a balanced well supplemented raw recipe that we have used for our cats, and due to health issues one of our cats can not have dried food of any sort. These are an exception. Let me tell you why..

WHAT ARE THESE LIKE?
These are what they say they are. They are pieces of raw sockeye salmon, wild caught, which are freeze dried. There are pieces of flesh along with some pieces of skin.

HOW ARE THESE TO EAT?
I put these in water for our cats because one of them can not have any dry food due to crystals in the urine that he almost died from once. That is why these are perfect. They take only a few minutes to rehydrate and they are raw and fresh smelling.

DID OUR CATS LIKE THEM?
Let's say that I am attacked when I open the jar to feed them these. They really love them and go a bit crazy when they eat the treat that I give them.

CAN YOU USE THESE AS CAT FOOD?
Due to the lack of taurine and a few other supplements, these can not be used for a daily food. Think of them as cat candy. They only get them as a treat, but they are good for them.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If you are really interested in high health for your cat, especially if you like the idea of raw food, these are fantastic. No additional ingredients, they are perfect as a treat, especially rehydrated.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS for these. They are a perfect addition to our household and we will buy them again.

text:
When I got this light, I got it to supplement a Finnex 24/7 planted plus light which I have on a large tank. The idea is that I wanted to have an extra light on for just a few hours that would augment in one area only and then shut off again. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
LENGTH
This light is about 16 inches long without the legs on it. It comes with two legs that push into the OUTSIDE holes. That will give you a few more inches of tank you can stand it on for each side.

CORD
The cord has a timer on it which is very basic. It allows you to control the level of white light, blue light, together light, and the timer of 3 choices of time.

WHAT I FAILED TO NOTICE AT FIRST
The thing that I failed to notice at first was that the cord has a join in it which allows you to unplug the plug side from the light side, so you can feed it up through narrow places easily, or replace one of the parts if you can get one.

PLUG
The plug is a very large transformer with rigid prongs on it. I mention this because I had a problem trying to get this through the back of my built in fish tank unit. It was too big to fit between the wall and the unit.

DON'T DO WHAT I DID
I spent a long time trying to figure out a way to get that plug behind the 90 gallon fish tank unit. I could not get it through and I could not get the light up through- finally I noticed that it had the connector. I felt very stupid. By disconnecting the cord halfway through, it was easy to feed the cord behind the unit and connect to the light on top.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
I have a Finnex Planted Plus light which I was using on this particular tank. That is not the one with all of the colors or timers, but it is a straight foward blue and white light. This little light is about 2/3 the size of that Finnex, but it is a very night clean light that really does bring out the colors of the tank.

ALGAE
I highly suggest you keep an eye on the tank that you use this on because algae has a tendency to grow fast with this type of light. I have it on six hour timer and it is working out well. I might have to completely turn it off some days as I am battling with hair and black algae. Due to the shrimp in the tank and snails, I can not use the algae additive I wanted to use to clear it up.

TIMER
The timer works well, but after a week or so, I find that I have to readjust it. It works, it just changes the time during the day that it turns on and off gradually. It is not a big deal. It still stays on for the six hours I have it timed for.

DIMMER
The power button turns on the white lights, then you can dim them to where you want them. Press power again, then it is on blue lights. Power one more time and you are at both blue and white. You can put the dimmer on that as well. The dimmer feature is fantastic. I really like that.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a nice clean light for the fish tank. They have a cord that connects so you can easily work it up through your unit, and the timer is a great feature. I like that you can dim the lights as well.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a great little light. It has more light than some of the brands I have worked with and even is a cleaner light than my Finnex planted plus without overloading the plants. Finnex does not have a dimmer on it, so having this one with a dimmer is much nicer for me.

PHOTO
I tried to get good photos to show you, but they are not turning out so far. I have one of the light itself that is not too bad, but not great.

If I get some that look good, I will try to remember to post them for you. This is a much nicer light than others I have seen in big box stores. I still like my Finnex 24/7 light best, but this one is a nice added bonus. I would buy it again.

title: Another ineffective Hartz product
text:
Wondering how Hartz even stays in the pet product business.
I am guessing it is from a lot of one-time customers!

We already knew to not use flea products from them, and not to buy their
catnip (it comes from China, and the last box infected an entire tub of
catnip I'd had of another brand with some sort of strange little bugs. I had
to discard a huge amount of catnip!). Now I am passing on this product too,
and will never buy Hartz items again.

We just used this for our two cats. While they had no visible ear mites,
both were starting to scratch at their ears quite a bit, which is often the
first sign of mites starting up. We always treat both cats at the same time
so we can mark it on the calendar.

Well, this product irritated their ears so much! I did the right amount of drops in
each ear (and this item is extremely oily). I rubbed it in, then carefully wiped off the outer
ear with a cotton ball to get any excess. I did this a couple times that evening, because
they'd flip their heads and get more oil on the outer edge. I didn't want them ingesting this
if at all possible, so was pretty diligent about wiping the outer ear.

By the next day, our older cat's ears were fiery hot to the touch! It was like he had a fever.
He was still messing with his ears, but this time, it seemed more from discomfort than itchiness.
He was also trying to rub his ears on the carpet, never a good sign. By the following day, his
ear was so red, I was afraid it was going to need a vet trip. I took a warm washcloth and gently
washed his ears off to get any remaining medicine off his ears as much as possible. I took a Q-tip to
remove what I could a little bit further in, but you can't go very far in on a cat's ear.

Our youngest one hid from me for the rest of the evening, and I can only assume that she too was
not feeling well from the medicine. Around midnight, I went into the bathroom and found that she
had thrown up all of her dinner (from around 5 pm) into a big pile on the bathroom floor. She felt
miserable! I cleaned her ears as much as possible too - she probably ingested a little bit though
since she hid for several hours.

This stuff must burn like fire to the cats!
I know a fungicide is going to be a little uncomfortable - medicine does have to work.
But it doesn't have to be so painful, and cause the cats so much misery.

Hartz needs to get out of the pet business, or stick to just making dishes or balls.
Most of their stuff comes from China, and I think it must have a lot of loose guidelines there for
purity of product.
I am DONE with all Hartz items. You've caused my cats problems for the last time!

They seem to like the pumpkin over the sweet potato, so I am glad that that is only in a few of the cans. They like the pool of broth that sits around the flaked chicken or tuna. We're kind of loving this bolstered furniture protector. And my we, I mean my 2 labs and 4 cats.

The item is packaged as a long tube of polyester filled soft squishy pillow and the protector material. The main material is the typical quilted furniture protector material- water proof quilted material on one side, lightly nubbed no skid material on the back. The spot that the bolster pillow is placed is a solid plain material. The pillow is zipped into place.

What I like:
--full length zipper
--I thought for sure it was going to be a pain in the rear to place tube pillow into the protector, but it was the easiest, quickest placement of pillow into casing that I have ever experienced. ZERO STRUGGLE. Good!
--Medium size 30"Lx31"Wx6H" is good size for cats and smaller dogs* (I have big dogs, but still works)
--quilted material is soft and cozy
--bolstered pillow part is soft and plush
--nice colors to choose from, matte look. I have navy blue; very nice.

What I dont like/have concerns over:
--material that bolster pillow sits in is basically like bed sheet material. If you have a digger, I am not sure how well it will hold up to it. Nothing has happened with mine, but I am skeptical. I have no concern over the quilted part.
--and by no means is this going to hold up to a chewer. It isn't meant to, but just keep that in mind.
--6" high pillow bolster--while soft and plush, might be too soft for your needs. I don't know what the norm is. It feels comfy to me, and my lab likes laying his big gorgeous block head on it. So I guess that says something :)
--price. I hate to say it, but it is the most expensive one I have seen on Amazon. Maybe this one is different enough to warrant price difference, but with such a simple design, I doubt it? I could be wrong, of course. If it fits your budget, great. I am not deducting rating from it, but I am bringing it up. I know we all already spend good money on our furry babes, and I just wanted you to be aware of the other options.

My thoughts/experience:

title: She Sat With Her Head In The Bag Frozen For Five Minutes
text:
We have a funny cat. She is pretty easy going and she tends to like everything except for turkey. Our last cat would not eat anything except turkey. When I saw this set, I thought it would be perfect. THAT was an understatement.

BAGS
The bags are sealed at the top and I cut them open with scissors so I can have the longest edges to pull when opening later and sealing with the zipper seal on them. They are pretty thick and keep the food dry.

FOOD QUALITY
The food quality is excellent. The shrimp and fish smell very appetizing, and the chicken also smells good.

DOES THE CAT LIKE IT?
Well, the cat went so berserk when I opened the bag of shrimp, she literally crammed her entire head into the bag, locked her jaw on the edge and refused to budge for FIVE MINUTES. I was laughing so hard, I could not stand it. She would not budge.

Finally I got her to let me in enough to push her head out, as her jaw was locked on the bag. She was not letting go. When I gave her shrimp, she leaped and danced so much, I could not believe it. She also did the same for the fish. The chicken she likes to, but the fish make her crazy.

WHAT DO I USE THESE FOR?
These are tidbits. I use these for giving our cat a snack to make her feel happy when she comes in from outside at night, or when dinner is late, or other reasons. I only give her about four or five pieces at a time, except when she knocks the bag out of my hand and manages to get her head stuck again.

THE BOTTOM LINE
These foods are VERY appetizing. Our cat loves to eat, but she rarely goes THIS nuts over food. She has loved all of the fish, and even liked the chicken too.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. These bags don't look like much, but they are freeze dried so they hold more than they seem to.

I tried to get a photo of this crazy cat with her head in the bag, but I couldn't. She held me prisoner.

title: My 20 lb dog and I LOVE this carrier
text:
I ordered this only because it had free returns if it didn't work out. I was concerned because my dog weighs 20lbs and I just wasn't sure he would fit. I am so glad I finally decided to give it a chance. It has helped so much.

My dog is a shih tzu, bichon Frise mix. On his heaviest day he weighs 20 lbs. From the base of his neck to the start of his tail he is 16" long and he is roughly 10" tall to his back area. He also has a very long tail, I didn't put that in the measurements. I ordered the medium.

His breed cannot take the heat or long hikes. At all!! I always end up having to carry him. It was difficult to go very far while carrying him on my own. This carrier has been an absolute blessing! Do I feel the weight of him on my shoulders? Well, yes, but, it's much better than the alternative. Night and day difference in fact. I could carry him for long distances this way compared to not having him in the carrier.

I just support him by his front legs and every now and then would adjust the shoulder strap a bit. The strap is nice and wide and distributes the weight really well. In my case I am able to let him back out to walk until he gets overheated/tired again so I do get a rest. I just lower him to the ground and he is able to walk right out on his own.

He has not shown any preference with having one or two of his front feet out of the carrier. I haven't tried all four feet in and probably won't. Not sure how well he would fit in with all four? He may but I won't be trying it. I have no need to hook him in or close the netting around him since he travels well without it.

The picture I added for the review he was just put in the carrier and was panting a lot. I should have taken a follow up pic of him no longer panting and relaxed and enjoying the hike after just a few minutes of being in there.

Our warmest hike was in the high 80's and humid and we were out a good hour and a half. When the hike starts to be too much for him I place him in the carrier. (It does help to have another person there to help put him in but not necessary). Even though the weather is hot/humid he stops panting and is very relaxed after a short time in the carrier. Which tells me he's not at all too hot while inside the carrier.

Without this particular dog carrier I would never be able to bring him along for this long of a hike with our summers. I wish I would have gotten it sooner. I also like the two pockets. It fits his water bottle and my cell phone nicely!

title: not grain free-- yay!, pricey but quality, 414 cals per cup
text:
Instinct is a quality brand. Made in USA. Wheat free but made WITH grains. We incorporate grains, so this is great. We aren't one for raw, but I'm ok with small addition- nutritional variety.

AS with ANY new food, to help avoid diarrhea & tummy upset, transition food over slowly. I use as a topper, puzzle treat, snuffle mat/nose work food.. so it is more like a treat. BUT if you are providing as a meal, add it in slowly.

A few year back I thought grain free was the way to go, and have since changed my mind. I remember going with Instinct as the ingredients are so healthy and rated very well. I always had two brands of food in the house. This was always one of them. Eventually I got away from it as at the time I think all the options were grain free (I don't recall), and/or Amazon may have stopped carrying what we got (this was before other online options)

In terms of pricing, it is seemingly high, but I had compared a few top contenders-- took a look at the amount of servings rather than price per pound. I looked at the serving of food we would give our dogs and price it that way. One cheap brand may have 50 lbs in it, but directions would have me serving them 8 cups a day (low calories, filler), for example. This one is 3-4 cups per day, or less if monitoring weight. 414 calories per cup. ALL that info is in the feeding description. If you have a tubby dog (my girl is on a diet) I give her less of her usual kibble, and my boy gets the typical recommended amount for that brand. So a good quality food like Instinct wont require as much food. There are many high quality foods out there, this is one of them. If you dont want to use it as whole meal, it can be used as a topper to their usual kibble.

We have used Instinct brand on and off over the years for our two labs. This is the first time trying the lamb variety, and first time WITH grains. I have a very picky boy and not so picky girl. Neither are all that food motivated, but I do engage them in some food based games. One of which is to utilize a snuffle mat and sprinkle kibble all through it. And/or I will sprinkle kibble in various spots for them to find. When one doesn't have food motivated dogs-- LABS- at that, it can be tricky to get their interest in something. They are usually excited enough about the game that the food is secondary. When it came time to present this to my boy, he had no interest in it. My girl was skeptical at first then seemed to enjoy rooting around the mat to find the kibble. Since my boy is so picky, I dont blame the food. He may eventually come around to it, or I may need to try another flavor. Lamb is new to them, hence why my boy is backing away.

Knowing the brand, and seeing all the good stuff in the ingredients, I think it is worth the try. It is nice that they have a variety of proteins available in addition to the usual chicken for those that have allergies and sensitivities.

The food is all stages, all sizes. The size of the kibble reminds me of adult dog food, so your super tiny doggos or pups may have trouble. Not sure, I just know I have seen what small breed/non large breed puppy food looks like and it is way tiny compared to this. I'll include pics.

INGREDIENTS:

Lamb, Menhaden Fish Meal, Oatmeal, Barley, Millet, Turkey Meal, Canola Oil (preserved with Mixed Tocopherols and Citric Acid), Dehydrated Alfalfa Meal, Ground Flaxseed, Freeze Dried Beef, Montmorillonite Clay, Natural Flavor, Salt, Freeze Dried Beef Liver, Pumpkinseeds, Freeze Dried Beef Heart, Carrots, Freeze Dried Beef Kidney, Freeze Dried Beef Spleen, Potassium Chloride, Blueberries, Apples, Cranberries, Vitamins (Vitamin E Supplement, Niacin Supplement, L-Ascorbyl-2-Polyphosphate, Thiamine Mononitrate, d-Calcium Pantothenate, Vitamin A Supplement, Riboflavin Supplement, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride, Vitamin B12 Supplement, Folic Acid, Vitamin D3 Supplement, Biotin), Choline Chloride, Minerals (Zinc Proteinate, Iron Proteinate, Copper Proteinate, Manganese Proteinate, Sodium Selenite, Ethylenediamine Dihydriodide), DL-Methionine, Freeze Dried Lamb, Yeast Culture, Dried Lactobacillus acidophilus Fermentation Product, Dried Enterococcus faecium Fermentation Product, Dried Aspergillus niger Fermentation Extract, Dried Trichoderma longibrachiatum Fermentation Extract, Dried Bacillus subtilis Fermentation Extract, Dried Kelp, Salmon Oil, Freeze Dried Lamb Liver, Freeze Dried Lamb Spleen, Freeze Dried Lamb Heart, Freeze Dried Lamb Kidney, Rosemary Extract, Dried Bacillus coagulans Fermentation Product.

FEEDING:
Ideal feeding amounts will vary by age, weight, and activity level so the guide below should be used as an initial recommendation. Divide the cups per day by the number of feedings per day. Be sure to always provide clean, fresh water. Along with dry food, we recommend feeding raw or wet food to help increase the amount of water in your pet’s diet.

Daily Feeding Guidelines (standard 8 oz dry measure cup): 414 calories per cup

ADULT Maintenance (cups per day):
5-15 lb: ½ - 1 ¼ cups;
16-25 lb: 1 ¼ – 1 ¾ cups;
26-50 lb: 1 ¾ - 3 cups;
51-75 lb: 3 - 4 cups;
76-100 lb: 4 – 4 ¾ cups

WEIGHT LOSS (cups per day):
5-15 lb: ¼ - ¾ cup;
16-25 lb: ¾ - 1 cup;
26-50 lb: 1 - 1 ¾ cups;
51-75 lb: 1 ¾ - 2 ½ cups;
76-100 lb: 2 ½ – 3 cups

PUPPIES (Except Large Breed [70+lbs as an adult]): Feed up to twice the adult maintenance amount.

Pregnant/Nursing Females: Feed up to three times the adult maintenance amount shown above.

Transitioning to Instinct: Always introduce a new food over a period of 5 to 7 days, mixing increasing amounts of Instinct with the current food each day. Visit the Instinct Pet Food website for more specific feeding recommendations and information on how to easily combine different forms of food.

title: Saved The Lives Of My Rainbows- VERY Thankful For This
text:
EDIT FEB 3 2023
My rainbows are still doing great. The ones who were on their way out are full of energy and swimming around with gusto. If I didn't know for a fact they were not doing well,, I would be tempted to think I imagined it. All of the fish in this tank are more energetic than ever. Even my kids have commented.

Just wanted to update for anyone interested.

ORIGINAL REVIEW
--------
I have had aquariums for quite a few years. Recently, due to some issues with a nearby tower, tanks on one wall have developed some issues and they have been nearly impossible to remedy. I tried everything, including cleaning out the entire tank and replacing the fish.

The direct result of the problem nearby is high increase in parasites. Nothing was working. This was hitting all of us including other pets and us humans too.

Once we got some remediation going on our house, this one tank was giving me issues. I lost all of my fish that I raised from babies and then lost another school and was down to two. I got one last school after cleaning out my tanks and revamping, but once again evidence of parasite activity was starting and I was really frustrated.

I saw this UV filter and got it right away. I had two fish which were already showing signs that they would not likely make it past the following week.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a pretty generic box. It has everything you need inside. You have to put the suction cups in the back and then choose your water distribution and assemble that.

ASSEMBLY
I decided instead of heavy current that I would turn this on the lowest flow I could and opt for the sprinkling spout on top of the water.

MY TANK SET UP
I have a 75 gallon tank which has two 110 filters and two heaters in it- one on each end. I also have a circulation pump for waves so the rainbows can swim for exercise.

HOW I USED THIS
After putting this in the water, I turned it on 24 hour mode for a week. The gentle stream is perfect for adding oxygen to the water. After the first week, I used the timer to put it on 8 hours a day mode. After a few more weeks, I will probably go to 4 hours a day mode.

WATER CHANGES
When doing water changes, I always turn off and unplug my units. I do water changes every week or every other week depending on how things are going.

ALGAE
I did not get this for algae as I have a very hungry algae eater so he polishes off any algae that grows. I find myself harvesting from my other 6 tanks to put in for him to eat anyway. I can not say that this is stopping algae growth because he never lets it get very far.

SUCTION
So far the suction cups are great. They are tricky to get into the slots on the back though. Take your time. It eventually works out, but can be frustrating.

CLEANING
This is easy to take apart and it is easy to replace the bulb when it is time. I have not tried to get one yet, but will look for one as back up soon.

DID IT HELP?
Here is what has me so excited I am near tears when I talk about it. I have a beautiful tank of rainbows from all over. When they started dying again, I could not believe it. My filters were all cleaned out, the tank was balanced and I was doing weekly water changes.

Still my fish that were dying were starting to show they were on their way out. It was just a matter of time before the whole school would be gone.

After running this 24 hour mode for several days, I was shocked to see a change in my fish. They were very active and energetic. The two fish that were hanging near the top and side were swimming a little more than they were. By the end of the week, All of the fish were behaving normal and energetic and none of them were acting sick.

It is the end of the 2nd week and so far all of the fish are showing beautiful color, acting all normal and full of life and for the first time since this nightmare began, they are doing well. I hope this continues.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This UV filter has been a godsend. My fish rarely have recovered from this parasite problem caused by a nearby tower. I can not go into it, but I know that is what happened without a doubt. This is a great filter

MY RATING
FIVE STARS does not seem high enough for my excitement about this filter I am really thankful to have this and so far it has turned around my tank for which I am thankful.

title: Good Choice for Older Dogs
text:
When your dog starts to advance in age, you need to be careful about what you feed him/her. Older dogs have special nutritional needs and a dog food formulated to meet those needs is Nutro Max Senior Recipe Dry Dog Food.

Let’s first look at the ingredients with this dog food. There is no corn, wheat, or soy, so that is a plus. The ingredient list is mostly good, but there are a few items I would rather not see, and I don’t like that actual chicken ranks sixth on the list. Still, compared to other dog foods on the market, what this food offers is easily better than average.

With this dog food, the kibbles are small. They are dry and crunchy and take little effort for your dog to eat. I have two dogs and the older of the two is eight years old. He likes this dog food as much as any and he eats it willfully and happily. His younger sibling finds it okay, too. She isn’t quite a senior dog yet, but there should be no problem feeding this to other adult dogs.

Nutro is a trusted brand in dog food. Nutro Max Senior Recipe Dry Dog Food is a good choice for older dogs. It contains ingredients that are designed for a senior dog’s digestive system and health needs and while it doesn’t contain the most stellar list of ingredients, it is still better than most and a good choice for dogs aged seven and up.

text: I LOVE how clear this aquarium is - it beats glass x10 over.  BUT there are a number of issues about this - the most serious is WHY the center bar down the middle of the tank is bowing - started just a little at first but it's getting pretty severe.  At some point that center bar is going to SNAP!!!!  I believe the bar is there for internal support of the lightweight acrylic.  I'm TERRIFIED that the sides will fall in when this snaps and I'll have 29 gallons of water all over the floor of my rented duplex.  (In my earlier review I said this about the center bar  "I suspect they made it this way to give the sides extra support and keep it from bowing."  ) So I was uncomfortable about the center brace even then.  Behind the support bar you can put in all your gadgets - thermometer,  filter, air hoses etc.  The front would be covered by the so-called cheap hood with space for a single bulb (not included but you can get a full-spectrum tube light for this so you don't need to worry about plants but I chose to remove the hood and instead purchase LED lights that hood on top of the aquarium (not submerged but pretty forgiving about getting damp).  That way I don't have to take off the entire hood to feed the fish.  I just tilt the light fixture a little bit and feed them. You can also remove them entirely if you want to.  IT IS A MAJOR PAIN TO CLEAN make sure you purchase tools specific for acrylic.  And good luck trying to get rid of some of that extra hard algae off the sides - it just sticks too good to this surface compared to glass.  I'm sorry they have not perfected Acrylic quite yet.  My next 29 gallon tank looks nearly identical but is glass.  And DON'T FORGET THE BOWING PROBLEM!!!!!!! SCARY!!!

Dog owners know that dog treats are a part of the dog caring and dog- loving experience. This is fine by me, since I think it’s good to have treats like this to alternate with the ones that are more pungent and that make my dog drool and with one that are longer- lasting, which these are not.

The best quality of these treats is the ingredients. There are only a few and they are mostly meat, with no grains. You can feel good about serving them to your dog and because there is a large number of treats per bag, they are useful when you want a quick reward to feed your dog or a fast, simple, and efficient bribe to get your dog to do what you want.

Treats matter when you’re a dog and quality matters when you’re a dog parent. These treats from Visionary are good treats for those times when you want something that’s small and quick that still maintains a good level of quality. I recommend adding them to your dog’s daily treat routine.

title: Very quiet, has adjustable flow
text:
I have this installed on a 5.5 gallon, standard tank.

This filter, while is was a bit strong for my old betta, is perfect for the new guy, now that my other passed away. (In other words, great for a healthy fish, not so much for an elderly fish.)

It is very nearly silent, which I appreciate. I like to hear a little bit of the water movement, but I'm not too fond of the motor noise in filters.

One of my few dislikes is the very short intake tube. I would like to have the option of extending it another 2". It's also not very efficient at getting debris out of the water after a water change.

It does have an adjustable flow. Again nice, but there's not a whole lot of difference between high and low. I'd like to turn it down to the minimum during feeding time, but "low" is still a strong enough flow to sink the floating pellets in a hurry. (It's just not strong enough to pull them into the intake tube.)

Beyond those little things, I do think it's a little overpriced, but then again, I have 5 other filters sitting around now and returned two ohers that couldn't be used/didn't work in that tank.

Overall, I'm pleased with this, and will probably buy another one or two to keep on hand for small tanks.

title: It’s early, but I’m impressed so far
text:
Among others, I have a Great Dane and an English Mastiff. The mastiff is only 10 months old, and nowhere near full grown, but has an enormous head, and thus enormous jaws. Nearly every toy I’ve purchased for him in the last 7 months has been utterly and completely destroyed in a few hours. There’s a couple toys that last a few weeks, but I had to stop giving him rope chews. He loves them, and used to just shred them for easy vacuuming every day. Recently he started eating the shredded rope, so I can’t let him have those, and went looking for something cloth-like without a squeaker** in it.

I decided to give these frisbee like things a try. He’s been ripping and tearing at that thing for several of the last 24 hours, and there’s not a mark on it, and no holes in it. He’s played tug with his friend the Great Dane, and they haven’t managed to damage it, even on the corners.

I bought 2 to start with, and today purchased 2 more. He will destroy it eventually, so I want to have a new one available every time to keep him chewing the RIGHT things.

**For those wondering why I won’t buy toys with squeakers in them: the noises they make are deliberately designed to mimic the sound of a small animal in pain or distress. This can reinforce the natural prey drive that every dog Osborn with. In dogs with a moderate to high prey drive, when that drive is stimulated by sound, it can increase the drive, and endanger smaller animals in the home. Since I have 2 chihuahuas, and neighbors who let their cats roam free, I prefer to discourage the prey drive, and reduce the risk.

title: Dangerous!! NO QUALITY CONTROL & Higher Phosphorous than Renal Failure cats should have
text:
Anyone with a cat with Chronic Renal Disease, should read ALL the 1-star reviews first!!! I do not know why this product is showing an overall 4+ review rating. I think that is more for the dog food, not cat food.

I ordered this canned food and as many mentioned, it smelled awful, but after a day, my cats ate it. What worked well is the hydrolyzed protein which basically breaks up protein smaller than normal which helps sensitive stomachs and aids easier digestion. With 4 cats with chronic renal disease in Stage 2, suddenly, the vomiting stopped, which was great! HOWEVER, the small expensive food cans had A Lot of bones too large for any cat to chew or swallow. My cats just spit them out or ate around them.

At first, I just threw them away, but after I bought another box of food, there were so many bones I started saving the larger ones. I had almost a full container before I accidentally knocked it over and lost in the drain. Still, you can see those I saved in the picture, with a pencil eraser as size comparison.

Read on and see other pictures of many people who posted 1-star reviews showing blue & white plastic pieces in their food. A LOT of issues with Quality Control!!! They say everything is upscale, quality and made in regulated facilities. PHOOEY!! No USA regulated facility would allow all of these foreign substances at dangerous sizes allowed in food that is NEVER recalled!!!!! Check the dates of the complaints!

Finding food these kitties will eat isn't easy nor cheap!!! At first I believed their marketing and ordered from Amazon. But the last order I received was from Chewy and was different. I called the USA office in Florida and was told it was only the packaging, so I kept it. But once I ordered it, I noticed it didn't smell the same, there were no bones...which I thought was good. However, my cats would not touch or go near the food. They ate the other formula...but not this one. That's when I went back to Amazon to check reviews. I WAS SHOCKED.

When I read others complaining about sharp large plastic pieces in the food, pictures of various blue plastic throughout the food, and others complaining that their cats wouldn't touch the new formula, plus people saying they too were told it was a new package only....I realized the USA office wasn't telling people the truth. That may not be their fault. The company may not be telling them the truth and they are just repeating what they were told.

This wet food should have been pulled from the market due to quality control issues and should not be allowed to be sold as it is very dangerous to cats. Upon reading all the 1 star reviews, I realized that the formula did indeed change in another big way. The old formula had salmon and lamb in it. The new formula has no salmon at all. Also newly included was pig liver and lamb lung. Major formula changes!! Cats were attracted to the salmon...now there is none. Not sure why but my 4 cats will barely touch this food now. I kept thinking they'd get used to it, but after one cat started getting weaker and weaker...and not eating either the dry or wet food...I panicked and gave some other food. OMG, the next day the cat was walking again!!! I felt horrible that the cat was just refusing to eat because of that food!!

That's when I went to check the dry food to see what was in it since they cats weren't eating it either. I had just bought the dry food, but they wouldn't touch it either. To my surprise, the ingredients was not written on the bag. HOW ODD!! I thought that was required in the USA??? I immediately realized this company does not operate with the same controls as a USA company. Since this is the only Renal food I know that does not require a vet prescription, I got very concerned they had virtually no quality control because all these issues had gone on for a long time. I immediately went out and bought new food at the vets office, and removed all this food & threw it away. I didn't even trust giving it to a shelter because I didn't trust it and wouldn't want any other cats to get sick from it.

I haven't found were to complain about the quality control yet, but its definitely NOT with the USA office in Florida .

DO NOT TRUST THIS COMPANY OR THEIR MARKETING BECAUSE everyone who has complained, has similar stories. Quality Control is not adequate if it even exist and it isn't worth hurting your loved pet over.

Amazon needs to separate the dog food reviews from the cat food reviews. And they need to separate the dry from the wet reviews. It appears the dog reviews are better than the cat reviews....at least I didn't see anything dangerous to the dogs like there are for cats. They can hide a lot of negative reviews by combining all the reviews for all of the brand!!! DO NOT GIVE TO YOUR CATS!!

title: Do your research first
text:
I'm very disappointed with the product. After researching for "the best" external filter canister, I went with two eheim products. I have the classic 250 ( 2213) and the Ecco pro for the 80 gallons. I purchased the Ecco pro because the Ehiem tend to be rated under their actual gallon size. I found that the classic which is good for 60 gallons struggles to keep my established (4 years) 55 gallon clean. I added the pro which covers 80 gallons.

1st recommendation: get a filter that's the next size up if ordering an eheim.

After nearly two years to the date, the gray circular part on the hood broke and the green plastic section under the gray circles which the hood attaches to broke right off. I'm waiting on an email from the company and I really hope they can at least send me replacement parts as I do not want to have spent $120 on a system. I was running dual filters (the classic and the ecco pro) to maintain the highest health of my tank and it worked great for the two years.

2nd recommendation: Do more research and find a brand that you don't have to order online.

Pros:
1. Established company
2. online ordering access
3. versatile with numerous filter media options
4. priming function with handle is super easy.
5. compact

Cons:
1. underrated for gallon size.
2. cheap plastic
3. online orders only (no local dealer for me)
4. expensive buy-in
5. hood fits delicately on the canister
6. hood collects plant matter
7. life of product

Overall, I really like the classic canister better than the Ecco, but the ecco has a GREAT priming lever that really made priming the line easy. I am super disappointed that the canister/hood only lasted 2 years.

title: Perfect For Plecos In My Tank (Shrimp too)
text:
I have quite a few aquariums with various fish in them. Many of my tanks have plecos. I have some ceramic homes for them which they love. This was a perfect addition.

HOW THIS COMES
This came with a nice bubble wrap around it in a box with some packing. Amazingly it was not chipped or damaged.

HOW TO PREPARE
Because some warehouses regularly spray for bugs, I would HIGHLY suggest you soak this and any other fish decor in a bucket of water for a few hours, emptying the water every 20 minutes or so. If any residue of that sort is on it, it will come off and not hurt your tank.

DOES IT WORK WELL?
My fish love this. I would even say that standing up or leaning up against another rock or raised surface in the tank would make a nice home for an apistograma or small cichlid. My plecos love this and are quick to explore it. No one has claimed it as their home yet, but they soon will.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is ceramic. It is fragile, so you have to be careful with it, but it does make a great addition to any tank with plecos, small fish, shrimp, or even small cichlids.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I like how this looks and the design is great with many exits which my fish prefer. They don't tend to like houses with only two entrances for some reason.

text:
The Kawapaw Dog Harness is a no-pull dog harness that is made of stretchy nylon fabric. It is closed via velcro and there are two metal loops that must be hooked to the leash to keep it closed.

There are a couple of design issues with this harness. I purchased a medium size harness for my medium-sized dog (14.4 pounds) and it is quite tight on him. Rather than just enough material to make an effective harness, I feel like there's just too much material than necessary, making it hot for the dog. Furthermore, the two metal loops must be looped in to the leash's carabiner for it to work, making it more difficult than it should to put on, especially if the carabiner is small.

The end result is that my dog looks like a hairy man wearing a very tight t-shirt (think Michael J Fox's Teen Wolf). As a result, he hates the harness and being difficult to actually get him to stay still to hook both loops up, I end up not using it at all.

title: Helpful Support For Aging Cat Especially
text:
I have been looking for supplements for our cats which help to strengthen the thyroid and support for digestion for our older cat. Let's see how this measures up.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This supplement is a powder. It comes with a scoop that measures a teaspoon per scoop. powder is not very fine so there will be specs of the supplement that mix with the food- not a fine powder. The smell is a bit fishy but so is flax so that is no surprising.

HOW TO GIVE TO CATS
The tricky part is READ THE INSTRUCTIONS. The scoop included is a TEASPOON. The requirements for most cats is only 1/8 TEASPOON twice a day or a max of 1/4 TEASPOON. That means you can not get lazy and just put a scoop into the food.

DO THE CATS LIKE IT?
Our one cat is not picky so she usually will eat this mixed into the food without any problem. Our elderly cat who has been experiencing damage from someone in our neighborhood who started poisoning mice and he ate some was not so thrilled at first. After it sits in the food for a while, it absorbs the liquid and then he will eat it with less protest.

ANY RESULTS?
I have to say that adding this to their food (we make their food using supplementation and raw food as recommended by the feline nutrition organization) it has been a great help to our aging cat as well as our younger cat. Their coats have improved and it has helped our aging cat to keep using his box successfully which has been a great comfort.

THE BOTTOM LINE
A nice big container, this supplement is more than enough for our cats for a few years (the expiration date is two years plus). A picky cat may not like it at first, but a less fussy cat should have no problems with it. We like it so far as it has helped a lot for our aging cat.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am happy to have this available. It is hard to see our beloved cat start to fade away just because of someone's negligence, but this has helped make his life more comfortable and helped keep him functioning better despite the challenges. I recommend this for dogs and cats. I can see where it would help dogs a lot too.

CHARGER

DO THEY TRIM THE FUR WELL?
The combs don't work well for our cat, but when we use just the clippers set on the highest setting with no combs, it works like a charm and trims her fur perfectly for summer time.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although this is a great set, the clippers is the main reason I got this. It works like a charm on the cat. She loves it and loves to be trimmed with it. Every other tool is attacked bitten and growled at.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a fabulous tool and I won't be without it.

title: Good Quality Food for the Young at Heart Pooch
text:
A good, quality dog food can take some effort to find. Most grocery stores carry only the budget- priced brands composed of by- products and artificial ingredients. To get a good dog food you need to visit a pet food store or turn to the internet and one good food available online is Natural Balance Whole Body Health with Chicken, Brown Rice, and Duck.

We try to feed our dog better quality food and Natural Balance is, based on its ingredients, a good quality dog food. I was a little hesitant to try this dog food, given my dog’s negative reaction to the last Natural Balance experience. But I went ahead and accepted the opportunity and haven’t regretted it. My dog took a little time to warm up to this food, but now he enjoys it and consumes every serving with little or no coaxing. The food doesn’t smell very pungent and you won’t even notice it from a distance. This could be part of the reason my dog doesn’t just dive right in, but like I said, he does like I well enough to eat and that is what matters.

My dog is not a puppy, but it’s fine to serve an adult dog a little puppy food here and there. This dog food has a good level of nutrition that easily meets or exceeds the needs of an adult dog. Yes, there are special ingredients meant specifically for a puppy’s growth but again, a little bit of puppy food won’t hurt. As my dog’s owner, I feel good knowing that he is getting a good level of nutrition without the artificial ingredients so common to the less expensive brands.

One thing to bear in mind with the packaging of this dog food is that the bag is not re-sealable. I like the bags of dog food that reseal with a simple press and slide of the fingers along the zip- lock style top. There is no such thing on this bag so you will need to supply a large clip to keep the food fresh or pour the food into a different container. Otherwise, while this is an expensive dog food, it does have the positive qualities that concerned dog parents want and it earns a recommendation from me.

text:
Or Shih Tzu had most of her teeth pulled in September and she is well healed now, eating her dry kibble with ease. I swear that she enjoys her food more these days but still am cautious with giving her treats. When the package of Bixbi salmon jerky arrived, she sniffed the box as though she knew the contents were for her, an unusual action, but she was right. She ignored the other packages and focused on only that one. Now I'd already given her a salmon jerky treat earlier in the day, a product she likes but does not go crazy over, so I was going to wait to let her try the new jerky. The one she already had is very crumbly, turning into a sawdust type of texture when it is broken into smaller pieces. Since she looked at me with her big brown eyes and emitted little cries, I cut open the bag and discovered that this jerky is more uniform in shape and it's texture is not crumbly or dusty. The strips were all intact and they were easy to break into smaller pieces. I broke down and have her an inch long piece after she did her lithe roundabout dance for me. This is clearly her treat of choice and Bixbi has found their perfect consumer.

The dog goes nuts over this jerky and has no problem chewing it with her molars and incisors.
