title: UPDATED-Works Wonders on Bratty Cats and Angora Rabbits As Long As The Preferred Person Uses It
text:
In our house, we have angora bunnies that have their own brushes. Their coats need to be brushed regularly, but sometimes our cat, a short haired tabby, will get a bit jealous of the attention that the rabbits are getting. Now that has all changed with the Perfect Coat Deshedder!

WHAT IS THIS DESHEDDER LIKE?
The handle of the deshedder is very solid. It is a dark aqua teal color with a black rubber grip that runs from the neck of the handle on the top to the grip area of the handle below that your hand has to use for gripping the tool. The handle is ergonomically designed and fits perfectly in my hand. There is a hole on the bottom that you can string a rope through for hanging up or hang through the hole itself on a large nail.

The head of the deshedder is bent over reminiscent of a razor, but at a bit larger than 90 degree angle from the handle. The metal part of the deshedder is a very substantial metal which looks like a razor scissor with its fine teeth and it seems like it would be sharp, but it isn't. The edges are not sharp and neither is the top or bottom of the metal plate that is used to run through the fur.

HOW DOES THIS DESHEDDER PERFORM?
I have to say that when I first used this comb on our short haired cat, I was not expecting anything miraculous. I was surprised, however, at the amount of fur that was coming out of his coat and how much nicer he looked. His fur was very soft and it did cull through the hairs on him to remove those that needed to come out. I got a substantial amount out but not so much that I was concerned that this was cutting his fur- it wasn't.

HOW DID OUR CAT RESPOND?
Our cat responded as if I was murdering him the first time I tried this on him. His face was so disgusted and irritated with me that our daughter was laughing really hard. That, of course, made him all the more indignant and he struggled and ran away from me.

Our daughter was taking a look at the tool when suddenly she looked down and our bratty cat was tapping her leg with his paw then pointing to his head. He wanted HER to comb him. He laid there for about 20 minutes relishing being combed with the deshedder AGAIN and it has been that way since.

DID THIS WORK FOR OUR RABBITS?
Our angora rabbits do best with a flat brush that has a lot of wire bristles in it, but I did try this deshedder on them and I must say that it worked nicely on them too. They have short haired heads and legs so I even used it there with success. Although I would use the brushes most often, I can definitely see a use for this deshedder on them when I needed to get into some areas that needed finer combing.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Well designed, easy to grip, and precise, this deshedder worked beautifully on our short haired cat as well as our long haired angora rabbits. It did take out a lot of fur that needed to come out but did not hurt our animals in any way. After they got used to it, they all seemed to like being combed with it and did not mind the activity at all. (Well, except our cat prefers one person over another of course). The deshedder is high quality and I am very impressed with it. It works better than any other similar comb we have used in the past and really improves our animals' coats.

I give this five stars.

UPDATE MAY 2016
Finally our cat has decided that he loves this comb so much that he does not care WHO uses it on him. I have to say it is now a serious blackmail device. Our cat can not be convinced to do anything he does not want to- until NOW. HAHA. All I have to do is show him the comb and he is a puddle of mush. Leverage- at last!

Needless to say this is still five stars.

title: Not My Dog's Favorite Treats but They Pass
text:
Dogs love treats. They love food in general, as any dog owner knows, but they particularly love dog treats, especially those that are meaty and pungent with a scent that only a dog could appreciate. Other treats, well, they get less excited over and a prime example of the latter is Good N Fun Smoky Barbecue Flavor Treats.

These beef hide treats are solid in structure and are long and cylindrical in shape. They are thin, so there isn’t a whole lot of treat in each piece. They are designed for long lasting chewing action, and that is their primary purpose. Give one of these treats to your dog and it could very well keep him/her occupied for ten, fifteen, or more minutes. This is very different than other dog treats, most of which are gone within seconds after feeding.

Good N Fun do last longer than other treats, and this is good. But the negative is that my dog just doesn’t get that excited over them. He hears me say the word treat, and he normally reacts with anxious anticipation. But he just doesn’t get into these dog treats. He doesn’t grab them vigorously from my hands, like he does with his favorite treats. And when he has the treats in his mouth, he will often drop them after a minute of chewing once something distracts him. The treats are just not that appealing, at least not compared to the best dog treats on the market.

This isn’t to say that these dog treats are a total bust. My dog doesn’t find them very noteworthy, but he does eventually give in and finish them off and the longer than normal time to chew means he is preoccupied longer than with other dog treats. If you happen to have a young dog or other dog that has a habit of chewing, the fact that the treats are chewy can also mean your furniture and other valuables are a little safer.

My dog loves his dog treats, but he is less than thrilled with Good N Fun Smoky Barbecue Flavor Treats. They have enough going for them to reward a small recommendation overall, but be prepared for a less than excited reaction when you feed these to your dog.

title: Works very well
text:
We have a kitty cat who adopted US about four years ago.
Despite trips to the vet, all her shots, etc etc, she had a problem
with watery eyes. The vet suggested that it might be allergies, and
gave us a suggestion for an allergy tablet. Not a bad idea, IF we could
get it down her! While no cat likes pills, this one makes it her goal to
be sure there is endless drama if you try to give her one, including
growling, barking at us (yes barking!), hissing and foaming at the mouth.
She is also masterful at making herself throw a pill back up if we managed
to get one down her!

We'd keep her weepy eye cleaned, of course, but she would also sneeze from time
to time, usually on us, or in the water dish - ew! After reading so many other
positive reviews, I decided to give this product a try. By the way, it was never
suggested by our vet, whom I suspect of being very pro-dog, and not fond of cats!
Anyway, within days of putting the small amount in her food (I mixed it in - haven't
tried just sprinkling it on top yet), her eye has become much better, and not one
sneeze to be heard!

The only change has been the addition of this Viralys to her meals, so the credit
has to go to this! It is even very cold here, when she normally gets small sniffly colds,
and nothing at all! Yay!

I don't know if this needs to be given daily or not, so once we were cleared up, I am
giving it to her a couple times a week, unless it seems like we need to go back to daily.
It is too bad there are not other scents/flavors. This has a definite fishy odor, which
they don't seem to mind. I have no idea how it tastes and don't plan to find out, but both
our cats prefer poultry to fish flavored foods, so wish they offered a chicken Viralys!
Maybe in the future...

Meanwhile, if your cat has endless sniffles, a weepy or damp eye, I highly recommend this one!

title: ciube style beds always a hit in my multi cat household, stackable

Cat cubes are like super posh boxes, and we all know how kitties love hanging out in a good box. I have a few of these cubes (different brands) and for the most part they are all the same, all similarly priced. This Friends Forever cube bed/house is a little shorter than some, but is otherwise same dimensions. The opening is generous, which is important for our multi (chunky) cat household.

Anyway, this is my third heater.

My first heater was a 5 W heater and might have heated the water but I had just recently got a 5 gal tank. At the time, I didn't realize that I could use my 1 gal as a QT tank. Next, I got a preset 25 W heater with an automatic shut off. This heater barely heated up the water during the day and at night it barely kept within 70*C. Brimestone didn't mind the heater but he would always stay near it and only come out for food. I was told that I needed to put it in a 5 gal and not a 1 gal. I suppose it just depends on the heater. Now I have this 25 W heater and Brimstone loves it! He swims around the whole bowl (I know there isn't much room to swim) and he's much happier now.

Review: My heater did not come with instructions or suction cups. It does a light that lets you know when it's heating. I do not have it completely submerged (only to the top of the waterproof seal). It's very easy to adjust but it does a little bit to change temperatures. I got lucky and it was near the temperature I wanted the first time. I've only had it for a couple days but so far, Brimestone and I really like it. If the second heater doesn't work out, I'll definitely buy another of of these!

Vitamins and Minerals (Minerals: potassium chloride, salt, zinc sulfate, ferrous sulfate, manganese sulfate, copper sulfate, calcium carbonate, potassium iodide, Vitamins: choline, Vitamin B-1, Vitamin E, Vitamin B-3, Vitamin B-5, Vitamin A, Vitamin B-6, Vitamin B-2, Vitamin B-12, Vitamin K, folic acid, Vitamin D-3, taurine. I like that the pate has a bit of juiciness to it. My 2 elderly cats prefer the more wet pates over the more dry pates. I often buy them ones that say on the front "with broth", or "with gravy"- but some, like this one, where although it just says pate, it just happens to have more visible moisture content (from the fish broth)- which my cats like! yay!

The pate comes directly out of the can, easily. I always just dump the can on a plate and let my kitties have at it. The pate doesn't stay in a firm mound, it spreads out since it is juicy. Since wet food is about all they eat these days, i just open up cans through the day as they request them. I am owned, I know. lol

I like that the "high protein, grain free formula" is primarily protein, and doesn't have a bunch of non grain ingredients added back to fill it up. Some non grain alternatives potatoes, tapioca, rice) can be high glycemic, which is a concern for some cats. Or just used as fillers- basically nothing they really need. Not sure what the inclusion of carrots in the recipe is for, but it is last on the food list. Protein sources are first, which is good.

I like that this is a product I can buy from Amazon, or pick up at some of my local grocery stores. The price is a tad high for me for a 3 oz can, but I buy whatever will make my elderly 17 year old kittens happy.

title: Alpine Scratcher heads the cats' favorite list!
text:
Wow! First of all, this was at our door two days after I ordered it. That was great.
They actually unintentionally made this a multi-purpose cat toy. It was packed well with lots of that brown paper for shipping. Our Egyptian Mau (Nascar) loves to play with paper, so that was an additional toy for him. Then of course, there is the wonderful
box that it all came in. What cat can resist a new box? From here on out, I will refer to this new scratcher as the CCAS, for obvious reasons.

That being said, we have scratchers of some sort in every room of our place. This keeps them from deciding the furniture looks like fun.Our smaller cat Katy loves cardboard, and loves to scratch at an incline, so this was a natural for her. We have the flat one [[ASIN:B0002ASD6G Cosmic Pet Cardboard Scratcher with Catnip]], but wanted to try this one too.

Ours came totally sealed up with a small bag of catnip included. There is a shiny mylar ball attached from the inside and visible to the cats through the circular cutouts on both sides. (Note that our Mau found this right away and was very interested in trying to get it out! At one point, he managed to pull it out enough to bite it and was trying to remove it. He turned the scratcher over instead. Since it is cardboard, no harm, no foul.) I sprinkled a light bit of catnip on the scratcher to see what they'd think of it first. Cosmic Catnip is their favorite kind anyway, so I did not anticipate any problems (even though the bag did not have any scent at all. Also, ours did not have the C/C label on it, like it is shown in the product photo).

I posted several photos of our cats' first encounter with the CCAS. I'll try to get some more with a clearer shot, but I wanted to catch the first reactions. It was popular right out of the box! Nascar was the first to try it out (because Katy was sleeping). He loved it! Now, you'll note in the background of my pics that you'll see an Emery Cat scratcher back there too (the arched one). My daughter bought that for Nascar for his birthday. We thought he'd love it. Nope! He didn't want anything to do with it. The texture of that one is VERY rough, like an emery board, and we think it was uncomfortable on his paws. He loved the feather thing that came with it, and that was all. It has sat taking up floor space for 4 months.

Nascar was after the mylar ball first, but then spent time climbing around on the CCAS, laying on it, scratching it and sniffing every square inch. He then went to play with the brown paper shipping material for a little while. By this time, Katy realized something was going on and came in to check it out. She was immediately on top of the CCAS, rubbing it, scratching it and enjoying it! Now, she scratched the opposite way than I thought she would... I thought she'd be on the floor and sort of drag down the cardboard. Nope! She sat on it at the back and scratched from the lowest part back towards herself! Oh well - as long as she likes it!

Both cats adored the mylar ball, and I think it would be fairly easy to replace once it comes off. There is a washer attachment underneath the replaceable scratching surface. I could see hiding a few more of the mice in there as well, just for fun.

I am SO happy we bought this one. They have been playing with it all night. Nascar has tried to chase Katy away from it, claiming ownership, even tho it is a share toy. (Note - we bought this for their Christmas gift (don't laugh - lots of pet lovers give their pets gifts!), but I was too weak. I gave it to them right away.) We are probably going to get one for downstairs too, just because they are enjoying it so very much.

I highly recommend the CCAS. You can use any kind of catnip with it that your cat likes, or leave the catnip off entirely.
It probably won't matter, because the cardboard is such an attraction for the kitties. The company also sells replacement cardboard inserts, so no need to buy the entire scratcher again either. All in all, a great value, great cat item, and results in happy kitties.

title: Great To Have In Case Of Power Outage
text:
When it comes to fish, power outages can be stressful. One thing that is most important is maintaining and oxygen level in the water of the tank. This pump is great for that.

HOW TO CHARGE
You take out the pump door and it leads to the USB charger. It is a micro USB port, not a Type C. It took a few hours to charge up fully.

HOW TO TURN ON
You press the solid screen top on the power button. That will turn on the unit. The bar at the top will light up green.

LEGS
The legs on this are rubberized to reduce traveling and vibration.

CLIP
There is a clip on the back of this pump so you can clip it or hang it instead of laying it on a table top.

HOW TO CHANGE
If you hit the power button a 2nd time, you will get intermittent setting which has the air flow for a bit then shut off again intermittently. A blue light at the end of the green bar will light up to show you that.

HOW TO SHUT OFF
A 3rd press to that power screen will turn off the unit.

CAREFUL
Be careful because after you shut off the pump, it won't turn on again for a while.

DOES IT PERFORM WELL?
This definitely performs well. I have a variety of tanks, so I can put in the air stone and tubing (with check valve) in one tank for a bit and then I can move it to the other (being careful not to turn it off).
I leave it on intermittent so it saves battery power.

NOISY?
This is not at all noisy, in fact I have plug in pumps which are noisier.

PROBLEM
This is VERY easy to accidentally turn on. You have to be very careful to not only carry it but also store it where it won't be accidentally pressed into the on position.

BATTERY LIFE
This will last part of a day if I have it on intermittent. I have not run it completely empty of power at this point, however. I always recharge after about 6 or 7 hours.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great pump to have handy for power outages. If necessary it can be recharged with a power bank if you have a few always ready to go.

title: Update- from a 5 star to 1 star after a few months.
text:
This has been updated at the bottom with more pictures at the end.
Original review:
I ordered two of the 40 inch size, even though I could have gotten a smaller one for the smaller dog, he would no doubt have taken over her bed and the big girl would be stuck with a bed too small.
Hers is just right for a 45 pound dog. She can stretch out or curl up, either way. The bumper is really nice as a place for their heads. My smaller old boy is 25 pounds, and it looks like he'd have been fine one size down, but the fact that he has unused space doesn't seem to bother him at all.
Since I've unpacked these yesterday afternoon, they've hardly left them! Usually when we get up in the morning, we find one dog snuck onto the sofa and the other sleeping on the recliner. They are not allowed on the furniture, but we overlook this every morning. This morning, they were still in their new beds! That says a lot.
The sherpa is super-soft, yet still looks like it's sturdy enough to hold up well in the wash. Their old beds were from a different company and I was happy with them for several years, but they were a hassle to wash because of the zip washable cover on the bumper part was hard to get the giant ring of pillow back in. This says the entire one piece is machine washable, and I have a big front loader so hopefully this will be an easier wash. It looks sturdy enough, as I wash them every few weeks on bath day.
Twice a year we take a long road trip and the dogs mostly sleep whenever we're in the vehicle, so it's important that these are pliable enough to fit side by side between the back seat and back door of a very loaded van, and I can tell these will be just fine as they are very pliable. They also need to be lightweight, as when we stop at night we will carry their beds into the hotel rooms, and these are much lighter than their last ones, so these will be great for traveling. If I have any future issues, I will update.
Update:
I've washed these beds several times, and the dog hair DOES NOT come out! I've literally just spent an hour holding the nozzle on the Dyson to every inch to make these somewhat descent to bring in the house. These will never be clean enough, and will end up staying on the outside porch. I will order new ones with washable covers, hassle or not taking them apart- it's worth it. It was roughly a hundred bucks for the two beds, and didn't even get 6 months use. The dogs still love them because they are comfy, but they hold every hair in range. Pictures at the end tell the story. First are when they were new, then after I've spent my afternoon trying to get the hair out- which looks like it caused the pilling, then last pictures are of the one I still have to do. You have to make the pictures bigger to get the whole idea.
Thanks.

title: Perfect Way To Protect Myself From The "Little Darlings"
text:
Everyone thinks their dogs are wonderful. Some people even feel they can do no wrong. As the landscape of our area has continued to change, people are moving in and out. That means new dogs.

Going for a walk can be a challenge. I had stopped trying for a while until I got this.

SIZE
The size of this tool is pretty good. It fits in the hand, hangs from the belt and has a handy wrist strap too. It is not too hard to grasp except with perhaps a slick glove in cold weather.

OPERATION
This works very well. The first button emits a siren, but it is not ear piercing. This is good for dogs that you need to startle in more than one way suddenly.

The 2nd button is for the high pitched ultrasonic noise that will stop dogs, but humans don't hear it. This is great for those dogs in your area that would be offended if the owners knew you were using something on their dogs.

The 3rd button is flashlight. It works well..

CHARGING
I found that this took a couple of hours to charge up, but it works quite a long time before recharging. Well, of course, that is because I only have to use it once in a great while. More use will run it down faster.

WHAT I USE THIS FOR
I use this for a combination of going for walks and my own yard. I have a yippy dog next door which kills rabbits and other small animals. I want him out of our yard, and usually he stays out. However, if he starts barking and coming over here, I use the silent mode. His owner does not know and I am happy.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is handy to have. It has made my walks more friendly again and my yard happier too. It helps avoid neighbors who get worked up if you use something against their little darlings.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I love that this is rechargeable and I love how portable it is. I have a new confidence in going for walks again.

[[VIDEOID:bffb80beb2b729b2dbe5da5123aa057f]] I have to admit, I had my doubts about a fabric and mesh pet carrier. We've always used the molded plastic kind with the metal grid doors.

This appears to be very well made. I didn't find any areas with unsewn seams, loose threads, etc. The mesh seems to be strong, and the fabric sturdy too. There is an adjustable carrying strap so you can carry it by hand or over the shoulder.

This claims to be airline acceptable. I know nothing about that, because I hate to fly and have no future plans to fly anywhere. I know it must mean as a carry-on pet, because this would not be sturdy enough for the luggage compartment.

It comes flat in a bag. It was very easy to assemble in only a few minutes.
The floor base looks like berber carpet, but is more of a polyester sherpa-style fleece. The cover zips off for easy cleaning, should your pet have an accident while in the carrier.

We tried both of our cats in there. Our long-haired part-ragdoll weighs about 8.5 pounds on a good day. He fit great. He was very comfy, was checking it all out, and didn't mind it at all. He did get a claw caught fo a few seconds, so definitely have a fresh toenail trim before using it.
Our other cat, a tuxie-tabby mix is a 12 lb boy who doesn't mind his carrier at all. He was a little harder to get into it, but that's just because he didn't know what it was, and we slid him in the top instead of unzipping the front. 😄 He fit just fine as well.

We sat it down and let them explore it. Our ragdoll decided it was as good a place as any to take a nap. I'd say we all approve of this carrier.

As it said in the title, I have SEVEN fish tanks. My fish vary from neons and other tetras, to rainbow fish and even Apistogramas. I try to vary their food. This bag looked perfect to round out my food storage.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This food is rated for medium to larger fish. It is made sort of like small Grape Nuts type cereal bunches. These are not hard like that though. They are hard enough to stay together, but will work well for the fish to eat.

HOW DO THE FISH LIKE THEM?
I have crushed some of these into smaller pieces for the smaller fish. I then blend the sizes depending on the tank. Every single fish I have loves these things. The fish continue to eat these up every time I feed them with this.

CONTENTS
The bag has more than enough food to get me through a couple of months with all of my fish. If you have less fish, this will last longer for you most likely.

ANY ISSUES?
I have not had any problems with clouding of water, refusal of food, or rotting in the tanks. The fish polish this off every time. Even the plecos come out to eat when drop these in.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a great food to round out a fish diet. I feed this to my fish every other day and they love it. For smaller fish, I crush some up for the smaller fish.

title: Flexible Scheduling and Portion Controls
text:
We recently needed to leave our cat alone for a week in the house. This was the first time we had to leave her completely alone and we had some concerns about making sure she had enough kibble during the day. I selected this feeder with that thought in mind. We ended up not using it during the time we were gone as it came too close to the time we had to leave (no time to learn how to use it) and we had someone reliable come to feed her anyway, but we have since worked with it and are pleased with it.

The idea behind this feeder is straightforward. It dispenses food automatically, portioned and timed as needed. There’s no real mystery there. However, this is more than a simple “dumb” feeder that spits out a cup of food every so often and has one setting. Multiple feedings can be set up and portion sizes are adjustable to make getting the amount right without a lot of guesswork. Everything is programmable so that odd times can be set up instead of setting the feeder to go off at fixed intervals or at specific times of day.

In use it works well. We can set it to feed our girl twice a day (it’s capable of more) which is plenty. She’d eat as much as we’d feed her if we gave her more, and weight control is an issue with her, so controlling the portion side is important for us.

Assembly doesn’t require much effort and in no time at all we had it ready to roll. The instructions are fairly easy to understand too, though the controls are straightforward.

This is a good automatic feeder and it will serve well when scheduled feedings are necessary without having to be around. It works as designed, does more than the average automatic feeder and is easy to maintain.

title: Excellent, High Quality, Easy to Clean Dog Bed
text:
We own and raise Goldendoodles, over the years we have had many dogs and, in turn, have owned countless dog beds.

There are certain things I look for when purchasing a dog bed. First the cover must not allow fluids quickly to pass through it yet also be easy to remove and launder. The cover has to be able to withstand our dogs pawing and circling looking for the perfect position.

The inner pad needs to be created of dense enough foam where it will hold its shape and not go flat nor lose its shape over time. Our dogs tend to like to lay in the same spot which with some beds cause them to go flat in those areas.

This bed is excellent in all of the areas of which I look for. The cover is both soft yet tough. We have had it in use for over two months now and have washed it several times with no problems. There is a hidden zipper on the bottom that allows for the cover to easily be removed and replaced.

The inner foam pad is far better made than the vast majority of dog beds. The stitching is very well done, the foam is dense and made to hold up for the long term.

This is an excellent dog bed that I definitely recommend.

title: Pros And Cons For My 2.5 tank (I Have A Lot Of Fish Experience)
text:
I have quite a few tanks. One thing I have been wanting is a decent 24 hour cycle light which fits my smallest tanks- a 2.5 nano tank.

HOW THIS COMES
This comes in a box which has a remote box built in line with the cord and plug. The remote is easier to access if you have an outlet strip up near the tank where you can see it easily. With a tank that has outlet strips in a difficult spot to see, this can be an issue when you want to glance at the settings.

SIDE HOOKS
The side hooks on the light slide in and out and they can come right out of the light if you pull too hard. That is not an issue unless you have a pet or child who might accidentally pull on them (or a stupid fish keeper on a bad day who we won't discuss right now.. LOL)

MY SET UP
I have a 2.5 nano tank set up with chili rasboras and blue eyed rainbow fish- the tiny ones. I have a single filter (only tank I have with one if I remember correctly) and some wood and simple moss on the tree inside.

HOW THIS WORKS
I set this at 8 am for the 24 setting at 8am. It goes on pretty bright and then works through a 24 hour cycle. IT does stay blue a long time at night- way after all of the other lights have gone dark. I have set my own 24 hour lights to get dark by 10PM or so. The dark period is not awfully long because at 6am it is getting light again.

PERFORMANCE
I like the lights. They seem a bit bright at times, or too long in duration, but honestly, the plants are growing better minus the overgrowth of algae I was having before. So, that is a good thing. Also, the fish seem more lively and active than when I had a simple daylight that went on and off every day.

THE BOTTOM LINE
Although I wish I could make the night rotation longer with no lights on at all, as this is, it is the best light I have had for my nano tank ever so I like it.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. I would like it better if it had a little longer dark period at night. Otherwise, it is a decent light and my plants are doing well as are my fish. And it fits my 2.5 gallon tank perfectly. I would by another one.

title: It will turn your aquarium orange - not good when it starts killing fish
text: I have six DoJo Loaches (yes I am crazy about them) in a 50 gallon tank and they are all about 1 foot long and still growing so they will get their own 100 gallon tank in the next month or two (it's on order),  If you've ever had more than one DoJo you'll quickly realize these are the toddlers of the freshwater fish community.  They also can jump out of the tank and be out of it for more than an hour and still survive.  Impressive but you need a screen on top of your tank.  Anyway.  I threw some of these in and they went for them like a pack of piranhas but as far as I could tell they just chewed them up and spit them all out because i had a tankful of wafers and the water turned ORANGE.  It was late (like 2 am) and I'm trying to decide what to do when one of the first Rainbow fish dies, then the second and a third.  I grabbed my biggest net and managed to get all but one or two of the rainbow fish out and moved to my Gourami tank - went back and got the rest of them on the second trip so no more died,  I ended up doing nearly a complete water change at 2 am.  So it's hard to tell if they didn't like them or they were just full but wanted to chew on something but whatever is in these wafers polutes the water badly.  None of the DoJo's died but I've had them jump out of their tank and not discover them for more than an hour - somebody told me they have 4 swimbladders so they can hold lots of air before they diedl  Now I'm seeing little squabbles between my Rainbow fish and the Gourami - I never realized how assertive the rainbow fish are but after living with a a pack of DoJo's for the last 6 months I think they've become easily adjusted.  Once I get the 100 gallon tank, I'll move the Rainbows and Gourami to the 50 gallon tank the DoJo's currently live in,  So they'll have a lot of room to spread out and away from each other.  So far nobody has gotten hurt but i am missing a Tommasi Loach (very rare) that usually keeps hidden in a cave and I have to force him out during water changes - now I can't find him  at all and it's really broken my heart.  I never liked the rainbow fish from the moment I got them - they are just so boring and only a few are colorful compared to my very sedate but beautiful dwarf Gourami - so I may see if one of the local fish stores will take them.  UPDATE:  Why did I not read my own reviews again and I bought these.  This time for 5 plecos since they  are supposed to like them.  Like my DoJo, they enjoy chewing them up into a powder and then just leaving it alone.  The fish don't seem interested eiither - so I then have several piles of bright orange powder on the botton of my tank that's going to raise an already problematic ammonia problem.  The leftovers get siphoned out today and I'll never use them again.  At least nobody died (I fed a smaller quantity and the Rainbow fish have all died.  And this time I didn't feed enough to turn the water orange - but I'll have to wait for the water change to see if it goes orange then.  Please avoid these, it looks like all ingredients except the orange dye are fine.

title: High flow, NOT adjustable
text:
After 24 hours, I'm updating my review. First, it seems to have stirred up a bunch of stuff in the tank, but it is not clearing the water. Tiny little particles are now throughout the entire tank, and it looks terrible. (This is a 6 week old, densely planted tank with one fish. It wasn't messy, or full of crud.)

The water is literally propelled out of the waterfall outlet, reaching a solid 2" in front of where it should be falling. The splash is so high, the top of the filter is collecting water.

I'm really glad these were on sale. They are NOT worth their reputation.

This filter seems to be working pretty well, but keep in mind, it's got a really high flow.

There is no motor noise that I can hear, just the sound of the water turning the biowheel. Some people might be annoyed by it, but I like the sound.

At some point, I will be customizing the filter media, but for now I just dropped some ceramic media into the well below the biowheel from the old filter.

The only downside to this is the fact that the flow is not adjustable, and it's blowing my Pea Puffer all over the tank. I will need to find a way to break up the current a little. I know the box says for tanks up to ten gallons, but it might be a little too much for anything less than 10 gallons.

title: FIVE STARS with a couple caveats  Just ordered a second one for HARRY!
text:
Here's a pic of my Tortie, Rowan, by her carrier and cat cube (looks at over a dozen cat cubes, LOVE this one, link below) and Harry, my newest addition six month old.

THIS CARRIER was the BEST I could find and I looked at over a dozen.

This review is re the carrier, but had to mention the cube because they both LOVE IT and best one I found.

HARRY LOVES to sit on top of the cat cube shown in link below. ROWAN likes to be inside.

https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B093T71RFL/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
After literally looking at over a dozen cat carriers, soft with mesh and hard plastic, I decided upon this one because my MAIN concerns WERE SAFETY and SECURITY.

If you have a dog that chews or a cat that claws and chews, they can make quick work of a soft carrier.

Some of the hard plastic carriers also had some downsides of doors not being secure.

HERE is why I chose this one and my experience so far:

SECURITY AND STABILITY - THIS is bulky, yes, BUT it will easily keep my young cat secure. If you have to leave your pet in a crate, carrier for even minutes, you want to know it CAN'T get out. Just make sure you latch this door and your pet isn't going anywhere.

SIZE - My young cats are still growing, but this crate will EASILY accommodate them full grown. I got them each their own crate, even though as they're still fairly small, it COULD hold them both.

INSIDE FLOOR OF CRATE - it doesn't come with any type mat, which was fine with me, but it really needs something. My cat LOVES this bed (bought her two) and it easily fits in this crate! So I just use her second bed in it if she needs to go somewhere.
https://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B07JXHNZGQ/ref=ppx_yo_dt_b_search_asin_title?ie=UTF8&psc=1

AND one of the BEST parts, they don't seem to mind being in them. The tortie sometimes just goes in and lies down on it (I have put her small bed in it as the floor is just plastic, but she seems to LIKE the plastic floor).

CONS:

While pretty straight forward re attaching bolts, and I did it alone with any tools (71, female, not handy), if you have any arthritis in your hands, wouldn't hurt to have an extra pair of hands. It would also help putting this up on a table or large counter, rather than putting together on the floor.

The instructions aren't really useful, but that was ok, I figured it out. PUT the door in FIRST, which seems pretty obvious, but make sure you snap that in first, then work on the bolts.

BOTTOMLINE: GLAD I got it, would get it again, and if SECURITY is your biggest priority and you want for more than a five min trip to the vet where you will be with your pet the whole time (soft mesh carriers? really?), THIS could well be the best carrier for you, even though it is bulky. My cat's safety was my biggest priority in choosing her carrier.

title: Arrived In A Nick Of Time- Long Haired Cat And Burdock Don't Mix (Plus A Caution)
text:
We have a long haired cat- the kind with the very very fine fur who is most like an angora bunny. When we first rescued her, she was a tiny kitten and her fur was not that long or thick. We had another short haired cat that she played with and loved to follow outside. He passed away, and now she is queen of the jungle- with very long thick angora fine fur.

She came in the house and I was horrified. Combing her is a task, but I keep up with it well. This time however, I almost cried- I did not know what to do. The burdock and little balls of velcro from another plant had completely matted her fur. No shaving, cutting with scissors or brushing was going to help her. I was very upset and then there was a sound outside. Amazon was dropping by a package. Inside was this life saver. Let's take a look.

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This tool is a very simple tool. It has a nice grippy handle which is easy to hold and use without losing grip on it. It has two sides. One side has only a four curved blades/brushes, and the other has six.

HOW DO YOU USE THIS?
The idea is that you drag this through the fur, and when you hit a matted area, the blades cut through, much like the principle of thinning shears that the barber or hair salonist will use on thick hair. It takes out some of the fur at the base allowing the mat to be easily broken up.

HOW DOES THIS PERFORM?
Unlike our last cat, this one gets overheated easily. Having this is a godsend. Not only did it take out about 2/3 of the mats and sticky weed balls, but it also thinned her fur out beautifully. She does not have to look like she came out of a newbies gromming chop shop like in previous years.

CAUTION
It is summertime when I am writing this review. That means it is hot out. We do not have air conditioning, but we have a lot of fans going. If you plan to use this tool on a fine haired animal, I highly suggest that you get in a location with no wind or you will be covered in fur and it will be in your room for a very long time.

HOW DOES THE CAT LOOK NOW?
It is amazing. This tool took out a great deal of the mats, thinned out the fur of our adventurous cat perfectly so that she is soft, and looks normal , but she is very happy to be cooler.

THE OBVIOUS QUESTION?
There is an obvious question some of you might ask- "Why not just keep her inside?" This cat can not be kept inside. She is an outdoor cat and we tried a few times to keep her inside, but our house almost did not survive. She loves it outside, so this tool allows her to stay out and keep groomed at the same time.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This tool is a godsend. We have both angora rabbit and a long haired cat with angora like fur which both need grooming often. This thins out fur perfectly for summer, and also keeps mats at bay. It does not hurt the animals at all and works really well and quickly.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. I am VERY thankful for this amazing tool. It literally has made things tons better for us and our animals this summer. I highly recommend this if you have an animal with tendency to mat and who could use some fur thinning in the summer heat.

text:
I have this L 7" pack of 2 CHICKEN rolls as well as the variety in Peanut Butter (9"). Both smell pretty good. The aroma piqued the interest of my curious labs. I can see why my babies were eager to check them out. Having the two flavors to review worked out well since I have two labs, and while one isn't a fan of peanut butter the other really hates it. When presented with both flavors, my girl opted for the peanut butter over the chicken and my boy opted for the chicken over the peanut butter. That made things easy :) My boy is so picky about food that I wasn't sure if he'd even like this, but he did. Because I have the two flavors, my reviews will be pretty much the same.

They BOTH enjoyed their treats- such delight watching them take one and find a place to eat it. I was particularly amazed that my picky boy enjoyed his chicken one as much as he did. He will sometimes take a treat-- like he is being polite-- and then go deposit it somewhere. Cracks me up. But with this, he really got into eating it. The next day he was given the other one. My girl loved her peanut butter roll. The rolls are long and dense. These are an occasional treat, or super special treat because they are high in calories (332.7 calories per roll!), and last 6-7 minutes (I timed). My dogs are not big chewers, but they chomped these down real easy. I could tell that they were able to chew and eat them no problem- they weren't swallowing big pieces, gulping it down. I am pleased about that.

I'm not upset that the treats didn't last long, so I just consider it a special treat. They really enjoyed them, so I will consider these again for their birthday or Christmas. Price isn't bad for a high value treat.

My labs had no problem chomping on these, and seemed to handle them well (didn't notice diarrhea or tummy upset). They sure look like raw hide, but they definitely are not. I triple checked, even picked up a piece to look at it closely. Phew. I mean, the packaging says as much, but the overall look threw me off. Nice treat!

title: Don't let the 'shock' in the title scare you!  You don't have to use it!
text:
These e-collars have a great minimalist design, and seem well made, the quality is great, set up was easy-peezy- just hooked them up to charge first, and we were ready to go! The fact that it's a 2-pack is what sold me, because I have 2 pups. I can easily switch between the two collars to train. I did have to quickly learn which collar was on who, when I accidentally used the remote on the wrong collar.
I have two little 'devils' that LOVE to bark. I've tried just about everything with no luck, which is when someone suggested I try e-collars. I've never used a training collar before. It's the 'shock' that scares me. I wouldn't put my pups through anything that I wouldn't put myself through, and I definitely wouldn't want to be shocked. BUT, this collar has a vibration option, which is what I was intrigued with. I've tested the vibration on myself, and I'm fine with using it on my pups.
Two gripes: I wish the straps had more 'tooth'. They loosen up too quickly and easily. I'm thinking about replacing them with nylon straps with more tooth. Also, I wish there was a stopper on the wrist strap, so that it could be secure on my wrist when I'm out training with them. I added a stopper I had lying around to it, so that I wouldn't have to worry about it flying off my wrist while training (see photos).
Overall, I'm glad I wasn't scared away from these because they are 'shock collars'. You don't have to use the shock button. I've never used it on my pups, and I really don't have to use these too often because they learned fairly quickly on these. They're a great deal for 2, especially when they go on sale!

Is it chewy, but soft enough to tear into smaller pieces. Not a traditional stringy, tough jerky. This is soft, easy to bite into. Ask me how I know ;) lol

Treats come in big pressure seal bag, weighing 2 pounds. I estimate there are at least 50, 4.5" jerky strips to a 2 lb bag. I had already doled out several over the past few days, and there were a few broken pieces at bottom of bag, so my count isn't exact but I am confident with 50. All looked fresh-- no molds. Looks great, smells great!

So how does it TASTE? Yep, I can answer this too. While I am not into munching on dog treats, I will try ONCE a bite of something dry or chewy. Never ever wet food. But I do take a bite so I can tell how hard or soft something is, what taste stands out, and if it is too sweet, or too salty depending on what piqued further exploration after reading ingredients. Trust I don't try everything, but items that don't appear to be super gross I will take a bit from. Also my LABS are more apt to try something novel if they seem mommy noshing first.

As far as um.. dog treats go in a jerky style.. the are mild flavored with quite an emphasis on salt. The addition of vinegar might amp up that flavor a bit, not sure. I can taste the briny bite of a "salt and vinegar" flavor. It is actually not bad, haha. Contains glycerin, which can be sweet, but I didn't pick up on that flavor. Contains smoke, but it is super mild in taste and aroma. It basically smells and tastes like what it is: a jerky chicken treat. For a dog treat, I wish I knew how much salt these contain. Since they are treat, and treated as such.. my labs aren't handed out treats day and night every day. Its more occasional, and it has more to do with the fact that one hates food, and one is on a diet.

The one who hates food, my boy.. he is a skeptical kid. He rarely LIKES a treat. I was surprised that he not only looked interested in what I had, but was first to take a jerky treat from my hand (see pics..his sister is still sitting n floor waiting). THEN he came back for more. So Mister Picky Pants likes the smell and taste of these treats. WIN.

My girl, who is dieting is less picky about treats. She is still picky about some foods, but she seems keen on being my #1 dog treat tester (after me, of course. I kid I kid! haha). She really likes these. I'm not sure she really tasted it she ate it so quickly. I then decided to tear up the jerky strip and sprinkle it into her slow feeder bowl (purple bowl in picture).

Ingredients seem good, seems to be the treat they are both most receptive to receiving, so that says something. I'm still not sure about the salt content (try one, its salty!), but since it is a treat and not a meal, it may be ok. It certainly lends flavor that they like. Also, I really like that the strips can be easily torn up for use as a reward treat, or for using in snuffle mats, slow feeder bowls, and other treat puzzles.

Any reservations about the saltiness is reduced in light of all the positives about this big bag of treats. Not enough of an issue to peg it down to 4 stars (if we had 1/2 star ratings, then yes). Since there are so many positives I give it a full rating. We will go through so few, so I am going to divvy up the bag into smaller baggies to store in the fridge. This may not be necessary at all, but I want to make sure we enjoy this entire bag no matter how long it takes for my two big babies to get through.

title: lightweight ceramic, sturdy elevation stand, works well for our needs
text:
Lightweight ceramic bowls in sturdy elevated stand. Small bowls, but work well for smaller heads. Stand seems to stay in place (I have it on a vinyl tablecloth).

I had a very specific need for this style of bowl, and it surprisingly met that need. I have two young adult cats that I recently adopted. We already have 2 dogs and a cat and we knew that the transition would be slow. I set the new cats up in my office with all their needs. Door closed so the resident fur balls can sniff through door with new furballs. Then, at some point every day I close off the resident animals in part of the house and let the new kitties roam the other part of the house. This includes a sunroom with a screen door. After roaming around awhile, I close them off in the sunroom (had lots of windows, and totally outfitted with floor to ceiling climbers. Cat dream house!). When I do this, I make sure they have some food and water out there with them. I need the food and water containers to be easy to handle, and preferably something I can grab all at once to empty/clean/refill. That is where this set of elevated bowls come in.

The bowls are ceramic but light weight. I needed this. I did not want heavy for my very specific use. The bowls are small but effective-- again, exactly what I needed for my specific use. The framework holds the bowls securely and is easy to grab the whole thing-- perfect for my needs. So.. so far it has met and exceeded my expectations.

I use much larger, heavier bowls as the main food bowls any other time-- especially in a multi cat household (prior to adopting these cats, we had recently lost our 2 geriatric babies at 18+ years old.). This would not be something I would use as sole feeding station unless I had one small cat. Basically, know what you need, the size that you need, and the degree of weight you prefer for your bowls.

I am pleased with this.

title: Poor Tool to Help Train Your Dog
text:
I breed and own Goldendoodles and have raised dogs for my entire adult life. I have learned some facts concerning barking that are important to understand - their in instinctual, protective barking used to communicate when your dog senses danger or used to alert you then there is what I’ll refer to a nuisance barking.

It’s the nuisance barking that as a caring pet owner we want to curtail and eliminate as much as possible. This behavior can come about for a whole host of reasons and the key is figuring out what is triggering it in your dog. Most of the time nuisance barking is attention seeking behavior and caused because your dog is bored. The key is not to feed into the behavior. If they bark like crazy and the response is you pay attention - even if it’s yelling at them - they achieved the desired result and the behavior was reinforced.

I have used multiple similar devices - both fixed units, such as this one and anti bark collars.

This particular anti bark collar is not effective. While there are sensitivity settings I found they are either far too sensitive, alerting when the dog moves or scratches, or not sensitive enough, not alerting when the dog barks. Either scenario will prove ineffective in training. Consistency is the key.

This is not a product I recommend.

title: (UPDATED)-Cats Are Like People, Except People Don't Lick Peppers Or Pretend They Are Dead With A New Toy
text:
(SEE UPDATE AT THE END)
Our cat has had quite a dietary journey. When he first picked our family to adopt, he showed up at the door and was absolutely frantic to eat. He even ate ears of corn that he dragged out of our compost. As we trained him to eat really good food (and yes, taught him how to catch a mouse, because he had no clue), our beloved Tom has developed quite a discriminating palette. In short, he only likes high quality food. He won't touch anything with grain in it anymore, and he really only likes the high quality stuff. He also is not a fan of food that has too much meal or legume protein in it.

WHAT IS THIS FOOD LIKE?
First of all, this food is packed in a vacuum sealed metallic colored bag. The bag, once opened, does not have a zip or reseal capability. It is best to close it with a large rubber band or put it into an airtight container. The food itself is quite dry. It does not have the usual fillers in it, and each piece is rather hard, although it is not too hard so that the cat can not chew it. Aroma wise, it does not smell overly appealing like some cat foods, but it is okay.

WHAT OTHER FOODS I CAN COMPARE THIS TO
We have had a variety of other grain free foods to compare this with:

[[ASIN:B00PAV2DQI Solid Gold Indigo Moon Chicken Holistic Dry Cat Food, Chicken & Egg, Grain & Gluten Free, Cats & Kittens of All Life Stages, All Sizes, 12lb Bag]] - We used to get him this before they changed their packaging and our cat would eat it for a while and then prefer other food. It was one of the few he wanted to swap out now and then. This food is from the same company.

[[ASIN:B00D0TEX9C Blue Buffalo Chicken & Duck Cat Treats, 2 oz Bag]] (we have tried this one in every flavor)

[[ASIN:B0018CJYCO Taste of the Wild Dry Cat Food, Rocky Mountain Feline Formula with Roasted Venison and Smoked Salmon, 15-Pound Bag]]

We have tried others, but those are the main varieties that we have used repeatedly for our cat.

HOW DID OUR CAT REACT?
Well, before I tell you that, I feel it fair to say that Tom does not like chicken. He does not like chicken as a meat fresh, or in cat food usually. Once in a great while he can be coaxed to eat chicken that is in cat food, but that is usually short lived. So, this food is chicken based and that was a risk, but we were willing to take it to see if he would eat it to add variety to his diet.

When Tom was sleeping, he was already full. He had eaten his morning meal, so I knew if he did not stick his nose up at this food in that state, he would be saying something significant. He poked his head up and sniffed the food and gobbled it from my hand. My husband, rather excited, ran right over to his bowl and put some more food in. Tom went over, sniffed the food, asked to be let out and then went on the porch and licked peppers. Okay, so he was full. I thought we would wait until later.

Later on, he approached the food, and sniffed and then went out and licked peppers. We have a half bushel of peppers on the porch that had dew on them, and he was apparently licking the water off of them. He prefers rain water to any other water, even though he has filtered water in his bowl.

Okay, our cat is weird, granted, but we were NOT expecting that reaction.

So for a couple of days, when we give him this food, he goes on the porch to lick peppers. He has never licked peppers before. But then again, when we tested a new toy with him, he would watch it go round and round and then fall over as if dead. So, we are not dealing with a typical cat here.

THE BOTTOM LINE
So far, not sure if it is the chicken, or if our cat is just being weird, but our cat gobbled this up at first, but now seems to be avoiding the issue. This could change at any minute. Although it claims to not have any meat by-product meals in it, there are three listings for meal on the package. I am not sure what that means. Meal is meal, isn't it? There are also quite a few types of beans and peas in this, perhaps another reason our cat is not enamored with it at this point.

Cats, as many of you know, are goofy finicky animals, so after I get done submitting this review, he could decide to go ballistic and eat this stuff like a starving creature. For now, well, he would prefer to go lick peppers. Um. Okay, then. Cats are like people- each one is different, but of course people don't lick peppers or pretend they are dead when you give them a new toy.

I will update if our cat changes reaction to this food. I am also trying another fish flavor of this food, and perhaps he will like that better. In any case, my current rating based on his reaction is THREE stars, but I will change if his future reaction to it changes, which is a good possibility.

UPDATE 10-8-16
After several days of disdain and preferring to lick peppers, and then the porch, and then turning his nose up at the chicken cat food, we finally decided it was time to try out the fish version of this food- the turquoise bag.

We put it in his bowl and waited. He ate a few morsels, got an angry look on his face and began meowing in a "yelling at your stupid humans"sort of voice. We tried everything. He would not stop.

Finally, out of trying anything, my husband put a handful of the rejected chicken version of this cat food in his dish, and the cat ate it all up and went outside... to lick the porch.

So, now, he does not want the fish version only, he prefers to have the chicken after two tastes of the fish. If we give him a few morsels of fish first, he eats them up (won't eat at all if you give him more) and then looks up and meows until we give him the chicken. You know- the one that he refused to eat until now?

What changed? Who knows? Like I said, our cat is a weird one, but he sure is entertaining and loving- just weird.

He probably says the same thing about us to his friends.

I will update when he decides he likes the fish too and if he still likes the chicken.

For now, I am changing this to four stars as he has decided he likes it, but only after a few morsels of fish flavor first.

In summary, two of my cats' love this food and dug in immediately. My skinniest cat that is about four pounds now, would not touch this. Despite his response, this food was a hit but it is expensive. It is good for kittens or adult cats who need the extra calories to put on weight.

title: 4 watt heating pad w/ fleece sleeve, double decker cube, bed w/ scratcher above, catnip included
text:
This review is for the "Playhouse" option.

We love K&H products. We have been especially keen on using their heating pads for several years now. Between our aging kitties, and even our well "insulated" *cough-fat-cough* tabby, they have all enjoyed luxuriating on a heating pad during the coldest days of winter. We don't keep a real warm house, so cozy spots are a must.

The heating pads are great. The level of heat is akin to the warmth left behind when someone has been sitting in a spot for awhile. They aren't the kind that get hot, which is good. They are very low wattage (4 watts) and produce a "barely there" level of warmth to the touch, but it is enough to allow a cat or dog to get warm, stay warm and not have to rely on their own body heat. If you have an aging or ill pet, know that this will help so much. They likely won't get over heated, but please make sure they can get away as needed. Not comfortable or safe to be too hot either. While it is instructed to be turned on and off when not in use, I have kept all of mine running 24/7 for a few months at a time. No issues, but that is up to you. Check out reviews for just their heating pads and see that it is mentioned by customers. For what it is worth, I am only comfortable buying heating pads from K&H, and would only do that with their products. I've just relied on this brand for so long, I guess I have built in trust? Hopefully it continues.

We also happen to love this style of cube bed. Well, my smaller cats do. Has always been hit and miss for my larger cats.
--These cube styles are amazingly sturdy (we have different brands, styles, and they all hold up). They come folded, just add insert to make base sturdy, then the "lid" which serves to further stabilize it but also creates a second tier. Here it is used as a scratching post, play area.
--The opening on this is smaller than some, so it will depend on your cat whether they will enjoy this or not.
--The interior pad is a zippered sleeve for the heating unit.
--There is a slit in the back of the cube to allow the cord to trail through for plugging in.
--The black fluffy sleeve is fleecy and soft.

This is the first I have seen a double decker with scratching pad in it. Know that it could be left out and simply use that space as a top bunk for sleeping. Just as a cozy blanket or other bedding. The scratcher has a solid bottom so it could just sit on the floor. It is well constructed pad. Also includes two little packets of cat nip. Cute!

The weather is just turning here in NY, so I will getting out my other K&H heating pads as well as looking for the best place for this. I am already thinking it will be most utilized by my ancient boy, Joey who is 18 years old and will likely want easy access to a heat source. He has a little arthritis so his comfort is paramount.

As awesome as the cube style beds are, the aren't huge. My only (mild) let down is that this is smaller than my other cube style beds. Not a huge difference (a little shorter, and a few inches less deep). For example, one of mine is 15"x 15"x 17" and this is, 12" x 14" x 15". It is perfect for my smaller cats (less than 10 lbs) but not sure my bigger tabby would try to sleep in in. Take note of the size of the sleeping area to determine if this is right for your kitties/small dog. I see that there is a bench style "duplex" also offered (longer, has two openings, optional divider insert, heating pad, and top tier is a padded lid). So just see what looks best. Love the other option too.

Packaging: small square easy open box with just this folded cube and supplies, as well as instruction leaflet. Box is a typical full color, glossy, box that you would find as if it were sold on store shelf. Excellent for gift. Of course, packed in a brown box for shipping.

Overall pleased. If we could do half ratings, I would go with 4.5 stars. I am pleased enough to go with 5, as I think it is a very good addition to our home, and I am pretty sure my old boy will be making use of this as the temps drop. The attention to detail is what I expect from K&H, and they do not disappoint. So 5 it is.

Take care :)

title: Easy setup, works well.
text:
Update: After like 2 months of use, it's having a meltdown for some reason. I keep it hooked into a surge protector and we've had no storms so it's not electrical on my end. This thing beeps often and spins around in full circles and since it wasn't designed to work in a full circle- it throws litter out the front all over the place when it does a full circle. Eventually I can get it to stop and go back to it's normal position but a couple hours later I hear non stop beeping and see it making circles and throwing litter out. This things gone crazy!

This was very easy to set up and it works well, with no major complaints. It also works without the app for those who don't use apps for things like this. I pushed the four feet in, put the tray in the bottom, filled it with litter, put the scent thing in the tray, and plugged it in and it cycled it to level the litter and the litter is like perfectly level once that's done. The next couple of days a couple of cats have gone #1 in it and it did a good job at sifting it into the tray in the bottom and I notice no smell around the box at all. The cats still currently prefer one of their old boxes as they hate change, but I'm hoping they realize this box is always clean and go to it in time.

SO functionality, this waits a bit after your cat is out and then it rotates very quietly to one side to dump the waste into the bottom and rotates a bit back the other way to level the litter. If you put your hand up to the doorway of it in this cycle, it will stop until it's sure there are no cats in/ around the box- great safety feature that works well.

This box looks nice and is well enough made. I would point out that it's maybe best suited for a small to medium size cat. It's not a tiny box and a large cat could fit in there but it won't be that roomy and our big boy seems to love to stretch out as he does his business so I think he'll probably never touch this box but the two smaller cats will possibly. So my recommendation is to keep at least a box or so in the house if you have multiple cats. This box does not count as more than one for multi cats, it still counts as just one box. Cats that are territorial might be upset by there only one box and start spraying around the house. Don't blame them if this happens, it's your fault for not having researched it first. Cats and their litterboxes are a delicate ecosystem that if you upset it, causes chaos. So be careful whatever you do or you'll upset the balance and have spraying everywhere.

Overall this is a pretty nice-looking, well-made, functional box, I do recommend it if you understand what you're getting into. There's always the possibility that your cat will want nothing to do with it so always have at least one box available.

title: UPDATE-Utterly RIDICULOUS- Behaved More Like Bugs Bunny Cartoon Than Pet Carrier
text:
PLEASE SEE THE UPDATE AT THE END OF THIS REVIEW FOR MORE INFORMATION.
Here is the original review...
-------------------------------------------------------------
I don't often rate things one star, because I try to think things through a variety of scenarios. I figure if it does not work for me, that does not mean it won't be great for others. In this case, however.. well, let's take a look..

WHAT IS THIS LIKE?
This thing comes in a plastic bag. There are absolutely NO instructions, NO place listed where you can find instructions, and no way to know what the heck to do with it. It comes all soft sided folded up like origami style. You are supposed to unzip zippers and rezip it all so that it magically becomes this wonderful pet carrier. It has lots of soft mesh screening, some small plastic poles/stays on the seams which come popping out no matter what you do. There is a reinforced mat in the bottom that will fold out so that this luxurious portable pet condo can be set up and little "Fifi" can enjoy and relax feeling so comfortable with two additional screened in porches while you wait for whatever. Yeah, right.

HOW DID THIS PERFORM
After 1 hour trying to make this work and the other members of my family wondering what the heck it was supposed to be for because it was so awful, I finally got it to point where this carrier was all zipped up, nylon poles popping out, and the sides opened up like little extended screened in porches and the handles were extended. I had already tried it zipped in the basic carrier shape, now it was time to test out this expanded capability. Let's see..

I put the cat in there. Oh my god. Did you ever see those Bugs Bunny cartoons where the characters all get in a fight and all you see is a cloud with arms, legs, paws etc going around like a tornado? That is precisely what happened to this bizarre pet carrier. The thing became like it was alive rolling around the floor as our cat proceeded to try to bite, claw, and destroy the entire thing.

Picking it up by the handles was a trip. Okay, imagine a tent outside on the ground. The poles are all in place and the tent is not staked to the ground. Now imagine, putting a handle on each side of the tent and lifting it up from the handles which are attached partway up the two opposing walls. What do you think will happen? Well, that is how this behaves with the animal in it.

WILL THIS LAST?
Well, it took me 20 minutes to get the cat out of the carrier. Yes, I said OUT. She was having so much fun in destruction mode that she was like velcro sticking to this carrier. I unzipped it all that I could and I could not shake this cat out of there. Every zipper being zipped was like a play toy and I got clocked with claws thinking I was playing.

At the end of 18 minutes, I was shouting, "Get out of the stinkin carrier, you stupid cat! GET OUT!" Finally with strong force I shook her out much to my husband's delight who was now laughing so hard others were coming into the room to see what all of the laughter was about.. Yes, they laughed too.

THE BOTTOM LINE
If I didn't know better, I would think that I was on a hidden camera show given this so-called carrier to use. I think that the only animal that this would carry decently would be a small one who is two inches from death, comatose and paralyzed from the neck down. Otherwise, the carrier is unstable, impractical, and frustrating to say the least. Vets do not have 20 minutes to pry your animal from this carrier, or they will at least charge you extra for it.

MY RATING
One star. If you are going to sell something as bizarre as this, you want to have some kind of instructions with it. You also want it to be stable- isn't that the idea of carrying an animal anywhere?
---------------
UPDATE
I have amended this review, because after another 40 min of work, a bunch of us finally figured out how to make this system at least work for carrying the cat in the carrier with the sides up. It still is not stable enough but it does work better- as long as the tiny nylon poles stay in place, which they don't want to do. We could get this into the car and the cat to the vet, perhaps, but it still is a challenge to get her our out of it and it really is not very stable for travel.

The expandable sides are good if you have to wait to give the animal breathing space and room to allow her/him to still play a little while you wait. Oh who am I kidding? Our cat would have this thing in tatters within a few uses. It just isn't that sturdy.

We still can not figure out what to do with the random hook and strap which has no loop or hole to put it in. We thought it might be to hold the floor into place but we can not find anything to hook it into. It could be to hook the animal to so they can play outside the carrier, but most small animals would just drag the carrier with them. It is very lightweight. With no instructions, well, we have no clue.

I am changing my rating to three stars just because it CAN work if you really work with it. I still wish it had instructions in it which would make it better and that the nylon poles didn't pop out of place making it LESS stable all of the time. I tend to want to put this at two stars, but the others are closer to three. So, the three is really two and a half. HAHA

We should not have to work THIS hard at an item to make it work.

title: The dogs loved this food as a supplement to their usual food
text:
My friend runs a foster home and puppies are a revolving door. Before feeding this to any puppies, I tried this for my friend's dogs to supplement with their other food and they loved this food.

The kibble is dark and pellet shaped. This food is made in the USA from ingredients sourced around the world.

The ingredients are Cod Head, Whitefish Meal, Coconut Flour, Lentils, Whole Dry Eggs, Tapioca, Chicken Fat (Preserved with Mixed Tocopherols (Vitamin E)), Flax Seed Meal, Menhaden Oil (Preserved with Mixed Tocopherols (Vitamin E)), Coconut Oil, Natural Flavor, Marigold Petal, Banana Powder, Marine Microalgae, Chicory Root, Dicalcium Phosphate, Lecithin, DL Methionine, Taurine, L-Lysine, Lactobacillus Acidophilus Fermentation Product Dehydrated, Oligofructose, Yucca Schidigera Extract, Sea Salt, Kelp Meal, Vitamin E Supplement, L-Ascorbyl-2-Polyphosphate (source of Vitamin C), Niacin Supplement. Biotin,  Thiamine Mononitrate, L-Carnitine, d-Calcium Pantothenate, Riboflavin Supplement, Pyridoxine Hydrochloride, Vitamin A Acetate, Vitamin B12 Supplement, Vitamin D3 Supplement, Folic Acid, Choline Chloride, Potassium Chloride, Zinc Proteinate, Betaine Anhydrous, Iron Proteinate, Selenium Yeast, Copper Proteinate, Manganese Proteinate, and Calcium Iodate.  

GUARANTEED ANALYSIS
Crude Protein,min  --> 30%
Crude Fat, min  --> 16%
Crude Fiber, max--> 3.5%
Moisture, max -->7.5%
Ash, max --> 7.5%Etc.

The ingredients are good except for the lentils —see my note below. Note that unless a dog has a grain allergy, it is not a good idea to feed them grain-free foods exclusively. The reason is that vets are finding an association between heart disease (such as canine dilated cardiomyopathy) and grain-free dog foods. This disease is mostly associated with the foods that have peas, lentils, other legumes or potatoes as their main ingredients and this food has lentils. Nevertheless, I feel it is okay to feed this food to a dog only to supplement a dog's diet and not as an exclusive meal. Note that puppy food tends to have more protein than regular dog food.

In summary, the dogs definitely enjoy this food and it is perfect as a complement to their regular foods.  I love that the bag has a Velcro seal to keep their kibble fresh. The current price of $21.99 for 5 pounds is pricey but still competitive.

title: actually works nicely
text:
The concept is simple enough... it pulls out and retracts and there's a slide-lock, like a measuring tape. The brilliant thing is I think this is well enough made it won't break after playing with it a few times. I haven't had it long enough to prove this point but Flexi has certainly been around that long and I haven't heard that they're rubbish.

Here's a few things about how I use mine. I bought it primarily for tracking. It's not legal for most competitive tracking events which require a 10 meter (~33 foot) long-line, but this 8 meter tape is more than long enough for practical purposes and you don't waste any time or your second hand line-handling. The tape, I guess it's nylon or polyester, seems to stay free of weeds and stickers unlike cotton lines that seem to grab everything. The line won't burn your hands either since you don't even touch the line.

I clip mine to a harness. I wouldn't like to clip it to the collar because the brake is not smooth. On a really soft dog, just the retractor can be perceived as a correction. But if the dog starts to take off, clicking the brake really slams them. With a hand-held line, there's no abrupt changeover from freespool to locked. The dog should have no problem slamming on their harness though. I just wouldn't do it with a collar.

A smoother brake would be a nice idea, but it's not clear it could be done without considerably more weight or expense. I imagine a lever type drag brake like on a big game fishing reel. It would be progressive but still able to stop the dog quickly.

The weight of this thing is a little high for a leash but not bad at all compared to a 30 foot biothane line. The bottom line is I wouldn't use it in lieu of a 6 foot leash but compared to tracking lines, I think it's a winner.

Update after a little more than 1 year -- My 26' Flexi Explore failed after a trip to the beach where it ingested some salt water and a little sand. The tape would sometimes fail to retract. I took it apart and found it was reasonably serviceable. I cleaned it out and put it back together with a dab of grease on the plate where the edge of the coil spring winds and unwinds (it's greased at the factory as well), and some light silicone lubricant between the plastic spool and the case. But I found that the leash still jams when pulled out to full extension and it won't retract without pushing the spool manually to unjam it. I reassembled it a couple times to try to get it right and had to give up. It will either jam at full extension or fail to fully retract. I took a star off for this failure. It might be repairable with a replacement spring, but the cost of a new one is low enough to consider it disposable after a year of frequent use.

Otherwise I have found the retractable so useful, particularly when I need one-handed control. I actually decided to take Flexi's seriously after reading about a patrolman in Afghanistan who uses a Flexi Giant -- why? to allow the dog to track on-line and still keep his weapon hand free. With a traditional 10m long-line, line-handling takes two hands. I track my dog in IPO and have to use a regulation 10m line, but otherwise I prefer the retractable for one-hand operation. I don't handle a weapon in our peaceful society, but I've often got my hands full with children or the things that accompany traveling with them. Most of my dog-walking for the dog's sake is off leash in rural or wilderness areas, so my leash use is often in urban environments where society expects dogs to be leashed. A short leash is ok, but for more than just a short walk, like when you're going to be out all day, for many, many hours with the dog, I think the dog appreciates a little more freedom than a short leash when the opportunity presents itself.

In any event, I'm ordering another Flex... this time probably going with the Giant version in hopes of getting a little more durability.

However, it is mostly associated with the foods that have peas, lentils, other legumes or potatoes as their main ingredients. Note that I did not see any of the "bad" ingredients in this food; however, I personally would only supplement a dog's diet with grain-free since the science is new even though I really like the ingredients in this food. I also believe variety is best for nutrition.

This food's first 15 ingredients are deboned chicken, egg, sweet potato, tapioca, chicken fat, natural chicken flavor, dicalcium phosphate, minerals, flaxseed, yeast hydrolysate, cranberries, blueberries, broccoli, dandelion greens, salt, etc.

A can is often too much food, but this serving size is perfect for using as a topper.

Soft dog food should generally be avoided, but it is fine if the food is made with quality in mind. Nutro Pate Steamed Chicken and Turkey Recipe is definitely a quality, soft dog food and its meaty qualities are certain to be a hit with most any dog.

title: Basic “toaster-type cover” for a 36” (preferably metal) crate
text:
I ordered this for the rescue organization I am affiliated with because this can be used to partially cover a crate during transport or to provide a segregation barrier for upset or sick animals. Since a 36" metal crate was not at our disposal, I used a plastic carrier that was of lesser size. However, this is really for a square 3 foot metal crate, so keep that in mind when viewing the photos.

This reminds of me a no-frills toaster cover. Just pop it over the crate and then adjust as necessary. There are no hooks or straps for securing to the crate whatsoever. Even if there were, the dogs would probably chew on that. However, having an elastic band with Velcro that can go across the outside bottom of the crate in front and back, would be good.

FEATURES:

- The top part of the cover has a "peep hole" that is Velcro'd shut and can be opened to expose a crate's carrying handle - see first photo. Unfortunately, the demo crate did not have a handle.

- The front has a flap that can be rolled up and Velcro'd to the top via the hanging straps - see second photo.

- The left side has a small pocket for incidental items like a brush or cell phone - see third photo.

- The right side has a panel that can be raised to expose a mesh panel. This is to let air into the crate while still providing a barrier. The panel has Velcro in two spots so that it can be rolled up halfway or totally depending on how much one wants to expose the crate to air - see fourth and fifth photo.

- The back is fully zippered (as is the front) and can be opened up as well.

Overall, this is a decent cover but there is nothing that will allow this to stay in place when moving the crate around other than gravity. The current price of $19.99 is reasonable.

Our other younger kitten is more prone to eat most things, except she is learning from Ghandi and has become a bit more fussy.

WHAT IS THIS FOOD LIKE?
